topic.about.title: About Phoenix MCP
topic.about.body:
Phoenix MCP lets AI agents work with your Home Assistant, safely. Each agent gets its own access key, and you decide what that key can see and do.

## Three ways to use it {#ways}

- **Agent Chat**: chat with an AI model right inside Home Assistant. You add an account with an AI provider, and Phoenix runs the agent for you.
- **An external app**: connect an MCP client, such as a desktop assistant or a coding tool, with an access key. The app's own model does the thinking.
- **Home Assistant's own assistants**: Phoenix can answer as a voice agent, run AI Task actions, or lend its tools to another assistant.

Whichever you use, the same checks apply, and the audit log records each action.

Related: [{{label:agentchat.title}}](guide:window.agentChat), [Connecting External Apps](guide:topic.connecting), [Voice Agent, AI Task or Assist Tool Provider](guide:topic.homeAssistantFeatures)

## The checks {#checks}

1. **Capabilities**: what kinds of things the key may do at all, such as control devices or edit automations. Each is Deny, Allow or Confirm.
2. **Permissions**: which areas, devices and entities the key can see and change.
3. **MESA**: how careful to be with each device: let agents act, ask you first, or keep them off it. By default it mostly warns. [{{label:settings.mesaModeEnforced}}](guide:window.settingsSafety#mesa-mode) makes the rules hold. It [doesn't cover every action](guide:topic.mesaRules#coverage).
4. **Approvals**: an action set to Confirm waits until you approve it.

Related: [What Agents Can Do](guide:topic.tools), [Security](guide:topic.security), [Running Phoenix](guide:topic.running), [Admin API](guide:topic.adminApi), [{{label:accessKeys.cardCapabilities}}](guide:window.capabilities), [How a permission is decided](guide:topic.permissionResolution), [How MESA Decides](guide:topic.mesaRules), [How an approval works](guide:topic.approvalLifecycle)

## Why not a long-lived access token {#token}

A Home Assistant long-lived access token acts as your user, across all of Home Assistant's interfaces. Anything holding it can do what you can.

An access key works only with Phoenix. It has its own permissions and optional expiry, and a rate limit on Phoenix's own connection. You can revoke it without touching your own login. Phoenix's connection doesn't accept Home Assistant tokens.

## Where to start {#start}

In the {{label:shell.tabAccessKeys}} workspace, select **{{label:accessKeys.setUpAgent}}**. The setup walks you through a key, its permissions, and either Agent Chat or an external app, then lets you test the connection.

Related: [How your agent connects](guide:wizard.choose), [Installing Phoenix MCP](guide:topic.install)

topic.adminApi.title: Admin API
topic.adminApi.body:
The panel is built on Phoenix's admin API, and you can use it too: from a script, an automation tool or your own app. Everything the panel does, the API does. These pages are for developers.

Related: [Access Key Endpoints](guide:topic.adminApiKeys), [Approval and Change Endpoints](guide:topic.adminApiApprovals), [MESA Endpoints](guide:topic.adminApiMesa), [Agent Chat Endpoints](guide:topic.adminApiChat), [Settings and System Endpoints](guide:topic.adminApiSettings), [Agent Endpoints](guide:topic.agentEndpoints)

## Signing in {#auth}

Every admin endpoint lives under `/api/phoenix-mcp/admin` and needs a Home Assistant administrator. Send any administrator's token, such as a long-lived access token, as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

- Without a valid token, Home Assistant itself answers `401` before Phoenix runs, with no JSON body.
- A signed-in user who isn't an administrator gets `403` with error `forbidden`.
- While Phoenix is still starting, every endpoint except the catalog answers `503` with error `service_unavailable`.
- Phoenix access keys (`phx_...`) can't open these endpoints. They're for agents only.

The admin API keeps working while the kill switch is on.

Related: [The administrator side](guide:topic.security#admin)

## Responses {#responses}

A successful call answers `200` or `201` with a JSON body, or `204` with no body. Every response carries `X-Phoenix-Request-ID`, which the audit log and Home Assistant's log also record. Responses with a body add `Cache-Control: no-store`.

Every change you make through the API adds one entry to the audit log, under the administrator who made it. Reads aren't recorded.

## Errors {#errors}

An error answers with a status code and this body:

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_request",
  "message": "English description of the problem.",
  "message_key": "adminError.badJson",
  "message_params": {}
}
```

- `error` is one of the codes below. Code against it, not the message.
- `message_key` names the panel's translation of the message, and `message_params` fills it in. `message_params` appears only when the message has values.
- Text from outside Phoenix, such as an AI provider's own error, comes with `message_passthrough: true` instead of a key.

| Code | Usual status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_request` | 400 | The request is malformed or a value is out of range. |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | Not signed in. Home Assistant normally answers first, as above. If Phoenix answers, `message_key` is `adminError.authRequired`. |
| `forbidden` | 403 | Signed in, but not an administrator. |
| `not_found` | 404 | The item doesn't exist. |
| `conflict` | 409 | The item's current state doesn't allow this, such as a name already taken. |
| `already_exists` | 409 | The item already exists. |
| `stale_version` | 409 | Another change landed first. Read again and retry. |
| `restore_unverified` | 409 | A restore was sent, but the result doesn't match. Check before retrying. |
| `precondition_failed` | 412 | A required confirmation or condition is missing. |
| `request_too_large` | 413 | The body is over 1 MiB. |
| `internal_error` | 500 | Something failed inside Phoenix. |
| `service_unavailable` | 503 | Phoenix is starting, or the feature is turned off. |

## Request bodies {#bodies}

Send a JSON object of up to 1 MiB. An empty body counts as `{}`. Phoenix reads the body as JSON whatever the Content-Type says.

| Problem | Status | `message_key` |
|---|---|---|
| Body over 1 MiB | 413 | `adminError.bodyTooLarge` |
| Body can't be read, or hasn't finished arriving after 2 minutes | 400 | `adminError.bodyUnreadable` |
| Not valid JSON | 400 | `adminError.badJson` |
| JSON that isn't an object | 400 | `adminError.bodyNotObject` |

Lists that page take `limit` and `offset`, both whole numbers of 0 or more. Each endpoint caps `limit`; a bad value answers `400` with `adminError.badPagination` or `adminError.paginationNonNegative`.

## IDs in paths {#ids}

- A domain is lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, such as `light`.
- An entity ID is a domain, a dot and lower-case letters, digits and underscores, such as `light.kitchen`.
- A device ID is Home Assistant's device registry ID.
- Any ID is at most 255 characters and can't contain `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, `&` or `;`.

## Permission states {#states}

The API names the four permission states differently from the panel:

| API | Panel | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `GREY` | N | No setting of its own; follows the level above. |
| `YELLOW` | R | Read only. |
| `GREEN` | W | Read and control. |
| `RED` | D | Deny. |

Related: [How a Permission Is Decided](guide:topic.permissionResolution)

topic.adminApiApprovals.title: Approval and Change Endpoints
topic.adminApiApprovals.body:
These endpoints handle what agents ask you to approve, and the changes they make: approvals, configuration history, recovery records, Needs Attention and the dashboard card catalog. Signing in, the error body and request bodies work as described in [Admin API](guide:topic.adminApi).

Related: [Errors](guide:topic.adminApi#errors), [Request bodies](guide:topic.adminApi#bodies), [How an Approval Works](guide:topic.approvalLifecycle), [What Changes Records](guide:topic.configurationHistory)

## Approvals {#approvals}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/approvals
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/approvals/{approval_id}
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/approvals/{approval_id}
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/approvals/{approval_id}/approve
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/approvals/batch/approve
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/approvals/{approval_id}/reject
```

Use these to review, approve, reject or cancel the actions agents are waiting on. The endpoints for one approval answer with this approval record:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` | The approval ID. |
| `access_key_id`, `access_key_name` | The access key that asked. |
| `tool_name`, `cap_name` | The tool held for approval and the capability it needs. |
| `args` | The tool's arguments. Secrets, device codes and every key starting with `_` show as `<redacted>`. |
| `diff` | The proposed change. |
| `status` | `pending`, `approved`, `rejected`, `failed`, `expired` or `cancelled`. |
| `created_at`, `expires_at`, `resolved_at` | When it was asked, when it expires and when it ended. |
| `approved_by_user_id`, `approved_at` | Who approved it, and when. |
| `closure_reason` | Why it ended without running, or why its run failed. Values below. |
| `result` | The tool's result after an approve. |
| `request_id`, `client_ip` | The agent request that asked. |
| `household_request`, `ha_user_id` | The household request flag, and the Home Assistant user behind the request. |
| `execution_started_at` | When an approve started running the action. |

`closure_reason` is your own reason for a reject, or one of these values:

```text
access_key_inactive        capability_denied
kill_switch                admin_cancelled
access_key_revoked         access_key_expired
phoenix_mcp_data_wiped     execution_interrupted
execution_failed           agent_chat_ended
agent_chat_wait_timed_out  integration_removed
recovery_review_replaced   phoenix_mcp_restarted
```

Related: [Approvals](guide:window.approvals), [How it can end](guide:topic.approvalLifecycle#outcomes)

### List approvals {#list-approvals}

Lists approvals, newest first.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | query, string | Only approvals with exactly this status. An unknown value returns an empty list. |
| `access_key_id` | query, string | Only approvals from this access key. |
| `limit` | query, integer | Default 50, at most 500. A larger value counts as 500. |
| `offset` | query, integer | Default 0. |

The response is `{ approvals, total, limit, offset }`. Each item in `approvals` is the record plus `in_progress`, which is `true` while an approve is running it, or until Phoenix closes a run that never reported back. Treat such a row as not actionable, even when its status is still `pending`.

Errors: the paging errors in [Request bodies](guide:topic.adminApi#bodies).

### Read one approval {#read-approval}

Returns the approval record plus `in_progress`, as in [List approvals](guide:#list-approvals).

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.approvalNotFound` | No approval has this ID. |

### Approve {#approve}

Approves the approval and runs the held action as the agent asked it. The endpoint takes no body and ignores any you send.

Phoenix checks the approval in the order of the error table below. Before running anything, it saves an execution marker to disk. If a run reaches the action and never reports back, that marker stays, and every later approve, reject or cancel answers `409`.

If the client disconnects, the action still finishes. Read the outcome from the record or the `phoenix_mcp_approval_resolved` event.

Approvals that MESA held for confirmation, and recovery reviews, skip the capability check. Recovery reviews skip the kill switch check too.

The response is `200` with the updated record:

- `status: "approved"` when the action ran.
- `status: "failed"` with `closure_reason: "execution_failed"` when the tool returned an error. This is still a `200`.
- `status: "failed"` with `closure_reason: "execution_interrupted"` when the tool sent the change but couldn't confirm it landed. Check the result before you retry. This is still a `200`.
- `result` is `{ tool_result, outcome }`. It adds `refused_before_write: true` when the tool refused before writing anything.
- An approval that already ended comes back unchanged.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.approvalWipeInProgress` | Phoenix data is being deleted. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.approvalNotFound` | No approval has this ID, or it disappeared while running. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.approvalProcessing` | Another approve is running it now. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.approvalExecutionInterrupted` | An earlier approve reached the action and never reported back. Check the result before doing anything else. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.approvalExpired` | It was past `expires_at`, so this call closed it as `expired`. Nothing ran. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.approvalAlreadyResolved` | Another request finished it first. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.approvalAccessKeyInactive` | The access key is no longer active. Phoenix closes the approval as `cancelled`, reason `access_key_inactive`. |
| 403 | `forbidden` | `adminError.approvalCapabilityDenied` | The capability is now set to Deny for this key. Phoenix closes the approval as `failed`, reason `capability_denied`. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.killSwitchEngaged` | The kill switch is on. Phoenix closes the approval as `cancelled`, reason `kill_switch`. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.approvalRecordFailed` | Phoenix couldn't save the execution marker. Nothing ran and the approval is still pending. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.approvalExecutorMissing` | Phoenix has no way to run this tool. Nothing ran. |
| 500 | `internal_error` | `adminError.approvalExecutionUncertain` | The run raised an error. Phoenix closes the approval as `failed`, reason `execution_interrupted`, and won't offer it again. |
| 500 | `internal_error` | `adminError.approvalOutcomeNotSaved` | The action finished, but Phoenix couldn't save its result. Phoenix won't offer the approval again and later closes it as `failed`, reason `execution_interrupted`. Its `approval/executed` or `approval/failed` audit row, with `finalization: "not_saved"`, says what happened. |

Three of those errors sound temporary but close the approval for good: `approvalAccessKeyInactive`, `approvalCapabilityDenied` and `killSwitchEngaged`. Fixing the condition afterwards doesn't bring it back.

### Approve several {#batch-approve}

Approves several approvals in order, one at a time, through the same steps as a single approve. The batch stops at the first approval that doesn't come back as `200` with `status: "approved"`. If the client disconnects, the running approval finishes and the rest stay pending.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `approval_ids` | array of strings | Required. 1 to 50 IDs, each a non-empty string, with no repeats. |

The response is always `200`:

```json
{
  "applied": [{ "approval_id": "...", "tool_name": "..." }],
  "failed": {
    "approval_id": "...",
    "tool_name": "...",
    "status": 409,
    "error": "conflict",
    "message": "...",
    "message_key": "adminError.approvalProcessing"
  },
  "remaining": ["..."]
}
```

- `applied` lists the approvals that ran. An approval that was already approved counts as applied.
- `failed` is `null` when every approval ran. Its `status` is that item's HTTP status. Its `error` is the item's error code, else its `closure_reason`, else `"failed"`.
- `failed` carries `message_key` and `message_params` when the item's error had them.
- `remaining` lists the IDs the batch didn't try.

The batch adds one audit log entry, not one per approval.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.approvalIdsNonEmpty` | `approval_ids` is missing, empty, or holds something other than non-empty strings. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.approvalIdsUnique` | An ID repeats. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.approvalBatchMaximum` | More than 50 IDs. `message_params.max` is 50. |

### Reject {#reject}

Rejects a pending approval, so the action never runs.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | Optional. Stored in `closure_reason`. |

The response is the updated record with `status: "rejected"`. An approval that already ended comes back unchanged with `200`. A pending approval past `expires_at` closes as `expired` instead.

Rejecting a recovery review also records that you checked it. If the recovery record refuses that, you get `409` `conflict` with one of the keys in [Act on a record](guide:#recovery-action).

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.approvalReasonString` | `reason` isn't a string. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.approvalNotFound` | No approval has this ID. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.approvalProcessing` | An approve is running it now. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.approvalExecutionInterrupted` | An earlier approve reached the action and never reported back. Check the result first. |

### Cancel {#cancel}

Cancels a pending approval. It works like reject, with `status: "cancelled"` and `closure_reason: "admin_cancelled"`. Send no body.

The response, and the handling of ended and overdue approvals, match [Reject](guide:#reject). The errors are the same except `approvalReasonString`.

### Claims and events {#claims}

Phoenix fires two events on Home Assistant's event bus, so a script can follow approvals without polling:

- `phoenix_mcp_approval_claimed` fires with `claimed: true` when an approve takes the approval, before the action runs. Data: `approval_id`, `claimed`, `timestamp`.
- It fires again with `claimed: false` if a failure before the run leaves the approval pending.
- `phoenix_mcp_approval_resolved` fires whenever an approval reaches a final status. Data: `approval_id`, `access_key_id`, `access_key_name`, `tool_name`, `status`, `closure_reason`, `approved_by_user_id`, `timestamp`.

A page that loads while a run is under way sees `in_progress: true` in [List approvals](guide:#list-approvals) and [Read one approval](guide:#read-approval).

Related: [Events for automations](guide:topic.running#events)

## Configuration history {#history}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/versions
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/versions/{version_id}
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/versions/{version_id}/restore
```

Use these to read the changes agents and restores made, and to put one side of a change back.

Phoenix records versions of these resource types:

```text
automation  script  scene      helper     dashboard  entity  device
blueprint   energy  config_entry  area    floor      label   category
```

Each version has an action: `create`, `edit`, `delete` or `rollback`.

Phoenix keeps the newest 20 versions of each resource. Raw text over 100,000 bytes is stored as `{ "content": null, "truncated": true, "bytes": <size> }`, and you can't restore it.

Related: [Changes](guide:window.changes), [What Changes Records](guide:topic.configurationHistory)

### List versions {#list-versions}

Lists recent changes across every resource, or every version of one resource.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `resource_type` | query, string | With `resource_id`, lists every stored version of that resource, newest first, without paging. |
| `resource_id` | query, string | Send with `resource_type`, or leave both out for the recent feed. |
| `limit` | query, integer | Recent feed only. Default 50, at most 500. A larger value counts as 500. |
| `offset` | query, integer | Recent feed only. Default 0. |

The response is `{ resource_type, resource_id, versions, total }`. Each item in `versions` is a summary:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` | The version ID. |
| `resource_type`, `resource_id`, `alias` | What changed, and its name. |
| `action` | `create`, `edit`, `delete` or `rollback`. |
| `access_key_id`, `access_key_name` | The access key that made the change. |
| `approved_by_user_id` | The administrator who approved it, or who ran a restore. |
| `timestamp` | When it changed. |
| `summary`, `summary_key`, `summary_params` | A short description, and its translation key and values. |
| `has_before`, `has_after` | Whether the version holds a before or after side. |

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.versionResourcePairRequired` | Only one of `resource_type` and `resource_id` was sent. |

The paging errors in [Request bodies](guide:topic.adminApi#bodies) also apply.

### Read one version {#read-version}

Returns one version in full: the summary fields without `has_before` and `has_after`, plus `before`, `after` and `request_id`.

It adds `restore_refusals: { before, after }`. Each side is `null`, or a reason Phoenix would refuse to restore that side: `yaml_tags`, `audit_only`, `template_incompatible` or `entity_missing`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.versionNotFound` | No version has this ID. |

### Restore a version {#restore-version}

Applies one side of a version to the live configuration. An empty body is fine.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `side` | string | Optional. `"before"` or `"after"`. Default `"after"`, or `"before"` when the version has no after side. |
| `expected_latest_id` | string or null | Optional. When set, the restore applies nothing unless this is the ID of the resource's newest version. |

Send `expected_latest_id` to make sure no other change landed since you last read the history. If one did, you get `stale_version`; read the history again and decide.

The restore runs with your authority as administrator. Phoenix records it as a `rollback` version, with you in `approved_by_user_id`. The audit log entry keeps the access key that made the original change, as `originating_access_key_id`.

The response is `200` with `{ "restored": true, version_id, resource_type, resource_id }`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.versionNotFound` | No version has this ID. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.restoreSideInvalid` | `side` is something other than `"before"` or `"after"`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.stringOrNull` | `expected_latest_id` isn't a string or null. `message_params.field` is `expected_latest_id`. |
| 409 | `stale_version` | `adminError.restoreStale` | `expected_latest_id` isn't the newest version any more. Nothing was applied. |
| 500 | `internal_error` | `adminError.restoreFailed` | The restore raised an error. |
| 409 | `restore_unverified` | `adminError.restoreUnverified` | Phoenix sent the restore, but reading the resource back doesn't match. It may be partly applied, so check before retrying. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.restoreNoConfigSide` | That side holds no configuration to restore. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.restoreYamlTags` | The version holds YAML tags such as `!secret` or `!include`. Re-create it by hand. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | a recovery key | A recovery record refuses the restore. The keys are listed in [Act on a record](guide:#recovery-action). |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.restoreToolReported` | The restore tool refused for another reason. `message_params.detail` holds its own English text. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.restoreNotApplicable` | The restore couldn't be applied to the current configuration. |

## Needs Attention {#attention}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/attention
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/attention/{kind}/{record_id}
```

Use these to find agent and calendar actions whose outcome Phoenix doesn't know, and to mark them checked once you have looked.

Related: [Needs Attention](guide:window.attention)

### List items {#attention-items}

The response is `{ items }`. Each item is one of these:

- An agent action whose outcome is unknown: `{ id, "kind": "agent", tool, access_key_name, started_at, dispatch_result }`.
- A calendar write whose outcome is unknown: `{ id, "kind": "calendar", tool, access_key_name, started_at, entity_id, "dispatch_result": "unknown" }`. Its `tool` is `<operation>_calendar_event`.
- `{ "id": "calendar_storage", "kind": "calendar_storage" }` when Phoenix can't read its calendar records.
- `{ "id": "audit_storage", "kind": "audit_storage" }` when Phoenix's last audit log save failed.
- `{ "id": "mesa", "kind": "mesa" }` when MESA failed to start.
- `{ "id": "mesa_rename", "kind": "mesa_rename" }` when a renamed entity's profile is in force but its save failed.

When a request wrote to a calendar, its calendar item replaces the agent item for the same request.

### Mark an action checked {#attention-review}

Records that you checked the outcome of one agent or calendar action. Use the item's `kind` and `id` in the path. Phoenix saves your review only; it doesn't run the action again or undo it.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `checked_outcome` | boolean | Required. Must be exactly `true`. |

Phoenix reads your user from Home Assistant again, and you must still be an active administrator. The response is `{ "reviewed": true }`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.attentionCheckRequired` | `checked_outcome` isn't `true`. |
| 403 | `forbidden` | `adminError.adminRequired` | You're no longer an active administrator. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.attentionNotReviewable` | `kind` is something other than `agent` or `calendar`. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.attentionSaveFailed` | Phoenix couldn't save the review. The action still needs review. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.attentionReviewConflict` | The action is still running, or someone already reviewed it. Reload the list. |

## Configuration recovery {#recovery}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/config-recovery
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/config-recovery/{recovery_id}
```

Use these to read the safety copies Phoenix takes before configuration writes, and to check, clear or restore them.

Related: [Safety copies](guide:topic.configurationHistory#recovery)

### List recovery records {#recovery-records}

Returns `{ records }`, newest first, without paging. Each record has these fields:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` | The recovery ID. |
| `resource`, `operation` | What the write changed, and how. |
| `access_key_id` | The access key that made the write. |
| `created_at` | When Phoenix took the copy. |
| `phase` | `prepared`, `dispatching`, `partial`, `unknown`, `verified`, `not_applied` or `reviewed`. |
| `before`, `source`, `expected` | The stored copies, and what the write was meant to produce. |
| `observations` | What Phoenix saw after the phase changed. |
| `reviewed_by` | Who reviewed it, once someone has. |
| `active` | `true` while the write is still running. |

Phoenix always keeps active records and records in `unknown`. It keeps the rest for 30 days, at most 20 per resource and 256 in all.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.recoveryStorageUnavailable` | Phoenix couldn't load its recovery records. |

### Act on a record {#recovery-action}

Inspects, reviews, deletes or restores one record, chosen by `action`.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | Required. `inspect`, `reviewed`, `delete` or `restore`. |
| `side` | string | For `restore` only. `"before"` or `"source"`. |

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.recoveryNotFound` | No record has this ID. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.recoveryUnknownAction` | `action` isn't one of the four. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.recoverySideRequired` | `side` is missing, or that side has no stored copy. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.recoveryManualOnly` | Phoenix can't restore this kind of copy. Restore it by hand. |
| 409 | `conflict` | a recovery key | The record refuses the action. The key names why. |

The recovery keys are `adminError.recoveryStorageUnavailable`, `adminError.recoveryOperationActive`, `adminError.recoveryCommandRunning`, `adminError.recoveryResolveInApprovals`, `adminError.recoveryFull`, `adminError.recoveryReviewBeforeRemoving`, `adminError.recoveryReviewBeforeRestoring`, `adminError.recoveryChangedAfterReview`, `adminError.recoveryAuthorityChanged`, `adminError.recoveryHelperUnreadable`, `adminError.recoverySnapshotUnsafe` and `adminError.recoverySnapshotUnsafeAt`. Any other refusal uses `adminError.recoveryBlocked`. `adminError.recoverySnapshotUnsafeAt` names the refused place in `message_params.location`.

### Inspect {#recovery-inspect}

Reads the current state of what the record covers. It never proves which request caused that state. The response depends on the kind of copy:

- A restart receipt: `{ runtime_replaced, "execution_attribution": "unproven" }`.
- A storage helper: `{ observed, helper_present, "execution_attribution": "unproven" }`.
- A Template helper: `{ observed, entry_present, "execution_attribution": "unproven" }`.
- Anything else: `{ "status": "manual_verification_required" }`.

### Review and delete {#recovery-review}

`reviewed` marks the record reviewed and answers `{ "status": "reviewed" }`. `delete` removes it and answers `{ "status": "delete" }`. Delete needs the phase `verified`, `not_applied` or `reviewed`.

Both refuse while the write is still running, or while a Home Assistant command Phoenix sent hasn't finished.

### Restore {#recovery-restore}

Writes the chosen side back. The record must be inactive, in phase `verified`, `not_applied` or `reviewed`, with a stored copy on that side.

- Phoenix restores storage helpers, Template helpers, Energy preferences, blueprint sources, and dashboard registry, layout and resource copies.
- Copies of configuration file text are always refused, because Phoenix doesn't write file text back.
- Every other kind, including restart receipts and Zigbee copies, answers `400` with `adminError.recoveryManualOnly`.

A restore answers `200` with `{ result, outcome }`, where `result` is the restore tool's result. A refused or failed restore also answers `200`, with `result.isError: true` and the tool's own text. Check `result`, not the status code.

## Dashboard card catalog {#card-catalog}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/card_catalog
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/card_catalog
```

The card catalog lists the custom dashboard cards a browser found. The panel sends the reports; you rarely need to.

### Read the catalog {#read-catalog}

The response is `{ harvested, entries, harvested_at, resource_count, failed_imports, resource_fingerprint }`. `harvested` stays `false` until a browser has reported. That isn't the same as having no custom cards.

Each item in `entries` has `type`, `name`, `description`, `documentation_url`, `preview`, `available`, `has_visual_editor`, `stub_config` and `source`. `source` is `picker` or `element`.

### Report a harvest {#report-catalog}

Replaces the whole catalog with what a browser found.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `entries` | array | Required. At most 500 entries are kept, one per `type`. A `type` is at most 120 characters. A `stub_config` over 2000 bytes is dropped. |
| `resource_count` | number | Optional. How many dashboard resources the browser saw. |
| `failed_imports` | array of `{ url, error }` | Optional. At most 50 are kept. |

Phoenix cleans every field and skips bad entries instead of failing. It reads the dashboard resources itself and stores `resource_fingerprint`, a SHA-256 over their types and URLs. The fingerprint is `null` when Phoenix can't read them.

The response is `{ harvested, harvested_at, cards, available, failed_imports }`. The last three are counts.

The panel reports at most once every 10 minutes per browser and panel version. It skips the report when it found no resources and no cards, and reports again only when more cards appear.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.entriesListRequired` | `entries` is missing or isn't an array. |

topic.adminApiChat.title: Agent Chat Endpoints
topic.adminApiChat.body:
Use these endpoints to manage the AI provider accounts Phoenix uses and to run Agent Chat turns from your own code. Every endpoint follows the rules in the [Admin API](guide:topic.adminApi) overview.

Related: [{{label:agentchat.title}}](guide:window.agentChat), [AI provider settings](guide:window.settingsProviders), [Errors](guide:topic.adminApi#errors)

## Provider accounts {#providers}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers
PATCH  /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers/{instance_id}
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers/{instance_id}
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers/{instance_id}/models
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers/{instance_id}/refresh
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers/{instance_id}/probe
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/probe
```

Add, check and remove the accounts Phoenix uses to reach AI providers. Conversation accounts serve Agent Chat, the Voice Agent and AI Task. Decision accounts serve the decision provider.

### Provider kinds {#provider-kinds}

Every account has a `kind`. Kinds with endpoints take an `endpoint_id`; the first value listed is the default.

| Kind | Purpose | Setup fields |
|---|---|---|
| `claude` (Anthropic) | conversation | `api_key` |
| `deepseek` | conversation | `api_key` |
| `chatgpt` (OpenAI) | conversation | `api_key`, `endpoint_id`: `global`, `us`, `eu`, `ae`, `au`, `ca`, `jp`, `in`, `sg`, `kr`, `gb` |
| `gemini` | conversation | `api_key` |
| `grok` | conversation | `api_key`, `endpoint_id`: `global`, `us` |
| `groq` | conversation | `api_key` |
| `kimi` | conversation | `api_key`, `endpoint_id`: `global`, `china` |
| `meta` | conversation | `api_key` |
| `minimax` | conversation | `api_key`, `endpoint_id`: `global`, `china` |
| `mistral` | conversation | `api_key`, `endpoint_id`: `global`, `eu`, `us` |
| `nvidia` | conversation | `api_key` |
| `mimo` (Xiaomi MiMo) | conversation | `api_key`, `endpoint_id`: `payg`, `token_plan`, `token_plan_sgp`, `token_plan_ams` |
| `tencent` (Tencent Cloud TokenHub) | conversation | `api_key`, `endpoint_id`: `singapore`, `guangzhou`, `silicon_valley` |
| `opencode` | conversation | `api_key`, `endpoint_id`: `zen`, `console` |
| `ollama_cloud` | conversation | `api_key` |
| `ollama` (local) | conversation | `base_url` |
| `openrouter` | conversation | `api_key` |
| `together` | conversation | `api_key` |
| `cerebras` | conversation | `api_key` |
| `fireworks` | conversation | `api_key` |
| `qwen` | conversation | `api_key`, `base_url` |
| `zai` | conversation | `api_key`, `endpoint_id`: `standard`, `coding`, `china` |
| `typesafe` (TypeSafe) | decision | `api_key`, `model` |

### Setup fields {#setup-fields}

Adding an account and checking a setup take the same body.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | Required. One of the kinds above. |
| `api_key` | string | Required for every kind except `ollama`. At most 4096 characters, with no control characters. Phoenix never returns it. |
| `base_url` | string | Required for `ollama` and `qwen`. Only `ollama` may use a private address. Every other kind uses a fixed endpoint and ignores this field. |
| `endpoint_id` | string | Only for kinds with endpoints. Leave it out for the default. |
| `model` | string | Optional for conversation kinds; leave it empty to follow the provider automatically. Required for `typesafe`: at most 200 characters, and in the provider's current list. |

### List accounts {#list-providers}

`GET /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers`

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `purpose` | query string | `conversation` (default) or `decision`. Any other value returns empty lists, not an error. |

The response has `instances`, the accounts, and `provider_types`, the setup forms. Both are sorted by label.

Each entry in `provider_types` has `kind`, `label`, `label_key` and `fields`. Each field has `id`, `type` (`secret`, `url` or `choice`), `label_key` and `required`. It may also have `placeholder` and `choices`, each choice with `value`, `label` and `label_key`.

Each account in `instances` has these fields. The API key is never among them.

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` | The account's ID, used as `{instance_id}`. |
| `kind` | The provider kind. |
| `name` | Made by Phoenix. It adds a distinguishing part only when one kind has several accounts. |
| `model` | The model a request uses now. |
| `model_mode` | `fixed` or `auto`. Decision accounts are always `fixed`. |
| `model_replaced_from` | A chosen model the provider has retired, or `null`. |
| `models_checked_at` | When Phoenix last read the model list. |
| `base_url` | As set up. |
| `endpoint_id` | As set up. |
| `capabilities` | Per model: what the provider declares, what a probe found, and options the provider refused in the last 30 days. |
| `capabilities_checked_at` | When Phoenix last checked capabilities. |

### Add an account {#add-provider}

`POST /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers` takes the [setup fields](guide:#setup-fields).

For a conversation kind, Phoenix runs the provider's credential check. For a decision kind, it loads the model list and requires your model to be in it. If that passes, Phoenix stores the account and tries to read its model list and declared capabilities.

The response is `201` with `{"instance": {...}}`, holding the account fields above.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerUnknown` | `kind` isn't a known kind. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerApiKeyRequired` | `api_key` is missing. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerEndpointInvalid` | `endpoint_id` isn't one of the kind's values. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.ollamaUrlRequired`, `adminError.providerBaseUrlRequired` | A required `base_url` is missing. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerUrlInvalid`, `adminError.providerUrlScheme`, `adminError.providerRemoteUrlScheme`, `adminError.providerUrlHostRequired`, `adminError.providerUrlCredentialsForbidden`, `adminError.providerUrlFragmentForbidden`, `adminError.providerUrlAddressForbidden`, `adminError.providerUrlResolutionForbidden`, `adminError.providerRemoteUrlAddressForbidden`, `adminError.providerRemoteUrlResolutionForbidden`, `adminError.providerRemoteUrlResolutionFailed` | `base_url` isn't an acceptable URL. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerConnectionFailed`, or a key for the provider's own failure | The credential check failed. `adminError.providerConnectionFailed` comes with a `detail`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerModelRequired` | A decision kind has no `model`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerModelNotListed` | The model isn't in the provider's list. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.decisionProviderRateLimited`, `adminError.decisionProviderTimeout`, `adminError.decisionProviderUnreachable`, `adminError.decisionProviderUnreadable`, `adminError.providerKeyRejected`, `adminError.decisionProviderCheckFailed` | The decision provider check failed: rate limited, timed out, unreachable, unreadable, key rejected, or another failure. |
| 409 | `already_exists` | `adminError.providerAlreadyConfigured` | An account with this setup already exists. |

### Change the model {#change-provider}

`PATCH /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers/{instance_id}`

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | string | The model to use. Conversation accounts accept any model ID. Decision accounts need one the provider lists now. |
| `auto` | boolean | `true` follows the provider's model automatically. Decision accounts refuse it. |

Send `model` or `auto: true`, not both, and no other fields. With `auto: true`, Phoenix reads the model list straight away, so the response shows the model it picked.

The response is `200` with only `{"instance": {"id": ..., "model": ..., "model_mode": ...}}`, not the full account.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.unknownFields` | The body has fields other than `model` and `auto`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.booleanRequired` | `auto` isn't a boolean. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerModelOrAuto` | Both `model` and `auto: true` were sent. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerModelRequired` | Neither was sent. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.decisionModelRequired` | `auto: true` went to a decision account, which needs a specific model. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerModelNotListed` and the decision provider errors under [Add an account](guide:#add-provider) | A decision account's model isn't listed, or the check failed. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.providerAccountChanged` | The decision account changed during the check. Read it again and retry. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.providerAccountNotFound` | No account has this ID. |

### Remove an account {#remove-provider}

`DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers/{instance_id}` takes no body. It removes the account and clears every setting that points at it:

- The Voice Agent's provider and model.
- AI Task's provider and model, with its entity and the Phoenix Assist pipeline.
- For the decision account in use: `decision_provider_id`, `decision_shadow_enabled`, all three tool review modes, and any `hybrid` routing mode, which turns `off`.

If you remove the default decision account, another decision account becomes the default. The response is `200` with `{"deleted": "<instance_id>"}`, even for an ID that doesn't exist.

Related: [Settings and System Endpoints](guide:topic.adminApiSettings#settings)

### List models {#list-models}

`GET /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers/{instance_id}/models` asks the provider for its models once. The response is `{"models": [...]}`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.providerNotConfigured` | No account has this ID. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerConnectionFailedNoDetail` | A decision provider can't be reached. |

### Refresh models and capabilities {#refresh-models}

`POST /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers/{instance_id}/refresh` takes no body. It rereads the model list and the declared capabilities, and stores them. It sends no completion requests, so it costs no tokens. For `ollama`, it sends one request per model.

The response has `models`, `capabilities`, `declared` (whether the provider reports capabilities at all) and `checked_at`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.providerNotConfigured`, `adminError.providerAccountNotFound` | No account has this ID. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerConnectionFailedNoDetail` | A decision provider can't be reached. |

### Check the model's options {#probe-model}

`POST /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/providers/{instance_id}/probe` takes no body. It asks the provider which options the selected model accepts. This spends credit.

Phoenix sends up to 10 one-token completions, plus one image check when image support is unknown. The result goes over the declared capabilities.

The response has `model`, `probed`, `calls`, `checked_at`, `effort_checkable`, `answered` and `vision_checked`. `answered` is `false` when the provider declined every question.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.providerNotConfigured`, `adminError.providerAccountNotFound` | No account has this ID. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerChooseModel` | The account has no model selected. |

### Check a setup {#check-setup}

`POST /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/agentcli/probe` takes the [setup fields](guide:#setup-fields), checks them and lists the models. It stores nothing.

A setup or connection failure still answers `200`, with the failure in the body:

```json
{ "ok": false, "error": "English description.", "message_key": "adminError.providerConnectionFailed", "message_params": {}, "models": [] }
```

On success the body is `{"ok": true, "models": [...]}`. A failure carries `message_passthrough: true` instead of `message_key` when the text came from the provider. `message_params` appears only when the message has values.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerUnknown` | `kind` isn't a known kind. |
| 409 | `already_exists` | `adminError.providerAlreadyConfigured` | An account with this setup already exists. |

## Running a chat turn {#chat}

```
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/agentcli/chat
```

Runs one Agent Chat turn and streams it back as Server-Sent Events. Note the path: it sits outside `/admin`, but still needs an administrator.

The route follows the kill switch. While the kill switch is on, it answers `503`. If the kill switch was on when Phoenix started, Home Assistant answers `404` until you turn the kill switch off.

Related: [Kill switch](guide:topic.killSwitch)

### Request body {#chat-body}

```json
{
  "access_key_id": "...",
  "instance_id": "...",
  "user": "turn off the kitchen lights",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}],
  "options": {"effort": "high"},
  "language": "en"
}
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `access_key_id` | string | Required. The access key the agent works under. It must be active. |
| `instance_id` | string | Required. The provider account to use. |
| `model` | string | Optional. Overrides the account's model for this turn. |
| `user` | string | The new message. Required unless you send `attachments` or `continue: true`. |
| `attachments` | list | Images for this message. See [Images](guide:#chat-images). |
| `messages` | list | The earlier turns. Phoenix doesn't keep the transcript: store the list from the `messages` event and send it back with the next turn. |
| `options` | object | Model options. See [Options](guide:#chat-options). |
| `continue` | boolean | `true` resumes a turn paused at the round limit, without adding a message. |
| `language` | string | The language for command routing. The panel always sends it. |
| `log_conversation_id` | string | Groups turns into one thread in the Conversation Log. |

The round limit is the `agentcli_max_iterations` setting. Reply style, detail level and Home-focused mode come from the Agent Chat settings when the request starts.

Related: [Agent Chat settings](guide:window.settingsChat), [How a command is routed](guide:topic.commandRouting)

### Options {#chat-options}

Phoenix uses each option only where the provider supports it.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `thinking` | boolean | Turns the model's reasoning on. Default `true`. |
| `effort` | string | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Default `high`. |
| `show_thinking` | boolean | Whether to show the model's reasoning. |
| `temperature` | number | The provider's sampling temperature. |
| `max_tokens` | integer | The most tokens the model may write. Default 32000. |

### Images {#chat-images}

Each attachment is `{"mime_type": "image/jpeg", "data": "<base64>"}`.

- Send at most 4 images, each JPEG, PNG or GIF.
- Each image is at most 2 MiB decoded and 8000 pixels on a side, and all of them together at most 4 MiB.
- The image's own header must match its `mime_type`.
- Images inside `messages` share the same 4 MiB budget. Going over it answers `413`.

This route accepts a body of up to 6,706,518 bytes. Everything except the images must still fit in 1 MiB.

### Errors before the stream {#chat-errors}

Phoenix checks the body size, setup, kill switch, access key, account, model, images and message, in that order. The first failure answers with an HTTP status. The [body errors](guide:topic.adminApi#bodies) apply too.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 413 | `request_too_large` | `adminError.bodyTooLarge` | The body, or the images, are over their limits. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.setupMissing` | Phoenix isn't set up. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.serviceDisabled` | The kill switch is on. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.setupIncomplete` | Phoenix is still starting. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.serviceStopping` | Home Assistant is shutting down. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.accessKeyNotFound` | No access key has this ID. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.accessKeyInactive` | The access key isn't active. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.providerNotConfigured` | No provider account has this ID. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.providerModelMissing` | No model is selected for the account. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.attachmentsInvalid`, `adminError.attachmentsTooMany`, `adminError.attachmentTooLarge`, `adminError.attachmentUnsupported`, `adminError.attachmentDimensions`, `adminError.attachmentsTooLarge` | An image can't be read, or breaks one of the [image limits](guide:#chat-images). |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.attachmentsContinue` | Images were sent with `continue: true`. They go only with a new message. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.attachmentsCompanion` | Images were sent with a Home Companion key, which takes text only. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.attachmentsVisionUnsupported` | The model doesn't accept images. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.invalidHostHeader` | The request's `Host` header doesn't form a URL. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.nothingToContinue` | `continue: true` was sent, but there's no conversation to continue. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.emptyMessage` | The message is empty, with no images. |

## Event stream {#events}

A turn that starts answers `200` with `text/event-stream` and the `X-Phoenix-Request-ID` header. Each frame is an event name and a JSON object:

```
event: assistant_delta
data: {"text": "Turning off the kitchen lights."}
```

Phoenix sends a `: keepalive` comment every 15 seconds. Once the stream starts, problems arrive as `error` events, never as an HTTP status. Fields marked optional appear only when they have a value.

| Event | Data fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ready` | `provider` (the kind), `model`, `access_key_id` | Always the first event. |
| `status` | `provider` (the label), `step`, `tools`, `phase`, `seconds`; during a retry also `attempt`, `detail`, `detail_code` | `phase` is `waiting`, `thinking` or `retrying`. Sent when a model call starts, on each change, and every 30 seconds while nothing else has arrived. |
| `thinking_delta` | `text` | Reasoning text, only when the provider streams it. |
| `assistant_delta` | `text` | Reply text. |
| `focus_declined` | none | The model declined a request outside the home in Home-focused mode. Phoenix removes the model's marker from the reply. |
| `tool_call` | `id`, `name`, `arguments` | Sent before the tool runs. |
| `tool_progress` | `id`, `message`; optional `message_key`, `message_params` | Live status of a long tool, at most every 2 seconds. |
| `approval_required` | `approval_id`, `tool_name`, `review_url`, `expires_at`, `diff` | The turn waits up to 900 seconds for a decision. |
| `approval_resolved` | `approval_id`, `status`, `reason`; optional `reason_kind` | `reason_kind` is `execution` when the approved action failed. |
| `tool_image` | `id`, `name`, `index`, `mime_type`, `data` | A base64 image from a tool result. |
| `tool_result` | `id`, `name`, `is_error`, `summary` | `summary` is shortened for display. |
| `usage` | `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `context_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens` | The provider's totals for the turn so far, only when it reports usage. |
| `notice` | `code`, `message` | `code` is `bad_tool_call_retry`, `max_tokens_stop` or `empty_turn`. |
| `continue_required` | `iterations` | The turn paused at the round limit. Send the next request with `continue: true`. |
| `error` | `code`, `message`; optional `retryable`, `outcome`, `diagnostic`, `message_params`, `provider_detail`, `provider_code`, `rate_limit`, `refused` | `code` includes `cancelled`, `internal`, `kill_switch`, `unauthorized`, `review_changed`, `outcome_unknown`, `output_limit`, `invalid_request` and the provider's own codes. |
| `messages` | `messages` | The full updated transcript. Keep it for the next turn. |
| `done` | `stop_reason` | Always the last event. `stop_reason` is `error` after a failed turn. |

Related: [Approval and Change Endpoints](guide:topic.adminApiApprovals), [{{label:agentchat.title}}](guide:window.agentChat#approvals)

topic.adminApiKeys.title: Access Key Endpoints
topic.adminApiKeys.body:
These endpoints manage access keys: creating them, changing their settings and capabilities, and setting what each one may read and control. Every path starts with `/api/phoenix-mcp/admin` and needs an administrator.

Request bodies, the error envelope and the ID rules work as described on [Admin API](guide:topic.adminApi). The error tables below list each endpoint's own errors. Body errors from [Request bodies](guide:topic.adminApi#bodies) apply to every endpoint that takes a body.

Related: [Errors](guide:topic.adminApi#errors), [IDs in paths](guide:topic.adminApi#ids), [Permission states](guide:topic.adminApi#states)

## Access keys {#access-keys}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}
PATCH  /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/rotate
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/stats
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/connection
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/audit
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/archived
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/archived/{id}
```

Use these to create, change, rotate and revoke keys, and to read their use. `{id}` is the access key's ID.

Every endpoint that names a key answers `404` when the key doesn't exist:

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.accessKeyNotFound` | No active key has this ID. |

### The access key record {#key-record}

Most endpoints answer with the key's record. It never contains the key itself.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | The key's ID. |
| `name` | string | The key's name. |
| `created_at` | string | ISO 8601 time. |

| `name` | string | Required. 3 to 32 letters, digits, `-` or `_`. It must differ from every active key's name, ignoring case and treating `-` and `_` as the same. Names of archived keys are free to reuse. |

### Revoke a key {#key-revoke}

`DELETE /access-keys/{id}` revokes the key straight away and moves it to the archive. The response is `204` with no body. Phoenix also:

- Removes the key from the Assist, Voice Agent, AI Task and Decisions bindings. An Assist pipeline, AI Task entity or Decisions entity that Phoenix created for the key goes too.
- Cancels the key's queued approvals and releases its MESA leases.
- Drops its rate-limit state and request counters, and removes its sensors.
- Fires the `phoenix_mcp_access_key_revoked` event with `access_key_id`, `access_key_name`, `revoked_by` and `timestamp`.

Related: [{{label:accessKeys.revoke}}](guide:window.accessKeys#revoke)

### Rotate a key {#key-rotate}

`POST /access-keys/{id}/rotate` gives the key a new value and takes no body. The old value stops working straight away. The key keeps its rate-limit state and counters.

The response is `200` with the record plus `access_key`, the new value. As on create, Phoenix shows it only once. Phoenix fires the `phoenix_mcp_access_key_rotated` event with `access_key_id`, `access_key_name`, `rotated_by` and `timestamp`.

Related: [{{label:accessKeys.rotate}}](guide:window.accessKeys#rotate)

## Presets {#presets}

```
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/presets
PATCH  /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/presets/{pid}
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/presets/{pid}
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/presets/{pid}/apply
```

A preset saves a key's settings so you can switch back to them later. `{pid}` is the preset's ID. Every preset endpoint answers with the key's record.

Presets are off by default. Turn on the `access_key_presets_enabled` setting first. Until then, every preset endpoint answers `403`, before it looks up the key.

A preset holds the key's settings: `caps` (all 32 capabilities), `persona`, `permissions`, `pass_through`, `use_assist_exposure` and `announce_all_tools`. It also holds `confirm_inline_wait_seconds`, `rate_limit_requests` and `rate_limit_burst`, plus its own `id`, `name` and `created_at`. The key's name and notes aren't part of it.

Each key holds up to 8 presets. A preset name is 1 to 40 characters after trimming, without `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, `&` or `;`. Names must differ within a key, ignoring case.

Every preset endpoint can also answer:

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 403 | `forbidden` | `adminError.presetsDisabled` | `access_key_presets_enabled` is off. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.accessKeyNotFound` | No active key has this ID. |

### Save a preset {#preset-create}

`POST /access-keys/{id}/presets` saves the key's current settings as a new preset and makes it the active one. The response is `201`.

|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Required. The preset name rule above. |

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.nameRequired` | `name` is missing. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.presetNameTooLong` | `name` is over `max` characters. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.presetNameInvalidCharacters` | `name` contains a refused character. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.presetNameTaken` | The key already has a preset with this name. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.presetLimitReached` | The key already has 8 presets. `message_params` has `max`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.presetSaveRejected` | Phoenix refused the preset as sent. |

### Rename a preset {#preset-rename}

| `confirm_pass_through` | boolean | Optional. Must be `true` when the preset turns pass-through on for a key that has it off. |

Before switching to a different preset, Phoenix saves the key's current settings into the active one. Applying the active preset again puts the key back to that preset's saved state.

Applying sets the persona, pass-through, Assist exposure, tool announcement, inline wait, rate limits, capabilities and permission tree. It also restarts the key's rate-limit count.

## Permissions {#permissions}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/permissions
PUT    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/permissions
PATCH  /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/permissions/domains/{node}
PATCH  /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/permissions/devices/{node}
PATCH  /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/permissions/entities/{node}
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/permissions/integration-options
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/permissions/bulk-select
```

These read and set the permission tree: which domains, devices and entities a key may read and control. Each node has a `state` and an optional `hint` for the agent.

```json
{
  "domains":  { "light": { "state": "YELLOW", "hint": null } },
  "devices":  { "<device_id>": { "state": "GREEN", "hint": "Desk lamp" } },
  "entities": { "light.desk": { "state": "RED", "hint": null } }
}
```

Node IDs follow [IDs in paths](guide:topic.adminApi#ids): domains under `domains`, device IDs under `devices` and entity IDs under `entities`. The states are in [Permission states](guide:topic.adminApi#states).

Related: [How a Permission Is Decided](guide:topic.permissionResolution), [{{label:accessKeys.permissionsTree}}](guide:window.permissions)
