`GET /access-keys/{id}/permissions/integration-options` lists the integrations you can use with [bulk select](guide:#bulk-select). The response is `{"integrations": [...]}`, sorted by title, domain and entry ID.

There's one row per config entry that owns at least one device or live entity without a device:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `entry_id` | string | Use this as `selector_id`. |
| `domain` | string | The integration's domain. |
| `title` | string | The entry's title. |
| `device_count` | integer | |
| `deviceless_entity_count` | integer | |
| `device_ids` | array | |
| `entity_ids` | array | Live, enabled entities without a device. |
| `registry_only_deviceless_count` | integer | Entities without a device that have no live state. |
| `required_domain_ids` | array | |
| `shared_device_count` | integer | |

### Bulk select {#bulk-select}

`POST /access-keys/{id}/permissions/bulk-select` sets one state on everything in an area, label or integration.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `selector_type` | string | `area`, `label` or `integration`. |
| `selector_id` | string | Required. The area ID, label ID or config entry ID. |
| `state` | string | One of the four states. |

- An integration sets its device nodes and the nodes of its entities that have no device.
- An area or label sets entity nodes only, for every entity whose area or label matches. An entity's labels include its device's labels.
- Existing hints stay. With `GREY`, nodes without a hint go, and nodes with a hint stay as `GREY`.

The response has the new tree and a summary:

```json
{
  "permissions": { "domains": {}, "devices": {}, "entities": {} },
  "summary": {
    "selector_type": "area", "selector_id": "kitchen", "state": "GREEN",
    "device_count": 0, "entity_count": 12,
    "registry_only_deviceless_count": 0, "required_domain_ids": [],
    "shared_device_count": 0
  }
}
```

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.selectorTypeInvalid` | `selector_type` isn't one of the three. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.selectorIdRequired` | `selector_id` is missing or empty. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.stateAllowed` | `state` isn't one of the four. `message_params` lists the `states`. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.permissionSelectionNotFound` | The entry doesn't exist, or no entity matches the area or label. Phoenix checks this before it looks up the key. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.accessKeyNotFound` | No active key has this ID. |

Related: [{{label:selectBy.menu}}](guide:window.permissions#select-by)

## Entity hints {#entity-hints}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/entity-hints
PUT    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/entity-hints/{entity_id}
```

Global hints tell every agent something about an entity, whichever key it uses. A hint on a key's own permission node wins over the global one.

Agents see the hint from the key's entity node first, then its device nodes, then its domain node, and only then the global hint. Phoenix removes text that looks like a secret, and replaces entity IDs the key can't reach with `<redacted-entity>`.

Related: [Entity hints](guide:window.permissions#hints)

### Read global hints {#hints-read}

`GET /entity-hints` answers with every global hint:

```json
{ "entity_hints": { "light.desk": "Desk lamp by the window" } }
```

### Set a global hint {#hints-set}

`PUT /entity-hints/{entity_id}` sets or clears one hint. The response is the whole `entity_hints` map. Phoenix checks the entity ID's format only, not whether the entity exists.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `hint` | string or null | Trimmed, at most 200 characters. `null`, `""` or no `hint` field clears it. |

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.badEntityId` | `{entity_id}` isn't a valid entity ID. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.hintString` | `hint` isn't a string or `null`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.hintTooLong` | `hint` is over `max` characters. |

## Entities {#entities}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/entities
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/resolve/{entity_id}
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/access-keys/{id}/scope
```

These show your home as the permissions editor sees it, and what one key can actually reach.

### Entity tree {#entity-tree}

`GET /entities` answers with every entity, grouped by domain and device. It isn't paged. Phoenix keeps the tree cached; add `force_reload` with any non-empty value to rebuild it.

```json
{
  "light": {
    "devices": {
      "<device_id>": {
        "device_id": "...", "parent_device_id": null, "name": "...",
        "area_id": "...", "area_name": "...", "entities": ["light.desk"]
      }
    },
    "deviceless_entities": ["light.porch"],
    "entity_details": {
      "light.desk": {
        "entity_id": "light.desk", "friendly_name": "...", "device_id": "...",
        "area_id": "...", "area_name": "...", "labels": [{"id": "...", "name": "..."}]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- Disabled entities, the `phoenix_mcp` domain and Phoenix's own sensors are left out.
- An entity with a state but no registry entry appears in `deviceless_entities`.
- A child device's main device appears in every domain where the child does.
- `person`, `tag` and `zone` are always present, even when empty.
- An entity's `labels` include its device's labels.

### Explain one permission {#resolve}

`GET /access-keys/{id}/resolve/{entity_id}` shows how Phoenix decides one entity's permission for the key.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `entity_id` | string | |
| `resolution_path` | array | `{level, state}` steps, outermost first. |
| `effective` | string | `WRITE`, `READ`, `DENY`, `NO_ACCESS` or `NOT_FOUND`. |
| `effective_hint` | string or null | The hint agents see, in the order given under [Entity hints](guide:#entity-hints). |

The `level` values run `global` (always `GREY`), `domain:<domain>`, then `device:<name>` for each device above the entity, main device first, then `entity:<entity_id>`. Device levels show the device's name, not its ID.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.badEntityId` | `{entity_id}` isn't a valid entity ID. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.accessKeyNotFound` | No active key has this ID. |

Related: [How a Permission Is Decided](guide:topic.permissionResolution)

### Key scope {#scope}

`GET /access-keys/{id}/scope` lists the entities a key can read and control.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `access_key_id` | string | |
| `access_key_name` | string | |
| `readable` | array | Entity IDs, sorted. |
| `writable` | array | Entity IDs, sorted. |
| `persona` | string | |
| `capability_flags` | object | The key's stored capability values, before pass-through applies. |

topic.adminApiMesa.title: MESA Endpoints
topic.adminApiMesa.body:
These endpoints read and change MESA: profiles at every level, deployment defaults, the tag vocabulary, issues and suggestions, and portable archives. Signing in, the error body and request bodies work as described in [Admin API](guide:topic.adminApi).

Related: [Errors](guide:topic.adminApi#errors), [Request bodies](guide:topic.adminApi#bodies), [How MESA Decides](guide:topic.mesaRules)

## For every MESA endpoint {#shared}

Every MESA endpoint except `device-options`, `integration-options` and `vocabulary` needs MESA running. While it isn't, they answer this:

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.mesaUnavailable` | MESA isn't running. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.mesaSaveFailed` | Phoenix couldn't save the change, so it undid it. |

Every change adds an audit log entry with the request path. Export adds one too, although it changes nothing.

MESA leases have no admin endpoints. Phoenix keeps them in memory, and agents request and release them with their own tools.

## Entity profiles {#entity-profiles}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/profiles
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/profiles/{entity_id}
PUT    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/profiles/{entity_id}
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/profiles/{entity_id}
```

Use these to find, read, save and delete the MESA profile of one entity.

Related: [Profiles](guide:window.mesaProfiles), [Levels](guide:topic.mesaRules#levels)

### List entity profiles {#list-profiles}

Lists stored entity profiles that match every filter you send, a page at a time. Inferred and unknown origins are included.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | query, string | Only entities in this domain. |
| `tag` | query, string | Only profiles whose effective tags include this tag. |
| `area` | query, string | Only entities in this area. |
| `origin` | query, string | `developer`, `user`, `hybrid`, `inferred_ai` or `unknown`. |
| `limit` | query, integer | Default 50. Values outside 1 to 200 count as the nearest end. |
| `cursor` | query, string | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. Leave it out for the first page. |

The response is `{ profiles, total_matched, has_more, next_cursor }`. Each item in `profiles` is `{ entity_id, document }`. Ask for the next page with `cursor` while `has_more` is `true`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.integerRequired` | `limit` isn't a whole number. `message_params.field` is `limit`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | none, `message_passthrough` | MESA refused the cursor or a filter. The message is MESA's own. |

### Read an entity profile {#read-profile}

The response is `{ entity_id, stored, effective, explanation }`:

- `stored` is the entity's own profile document, or `null` when it has none.
- `effective` is the profile MESA applies after combining every level.
- `explanation` is MESA's account of how it got there.

Related: [How profiles combine](guide:topic.mesaRules#combining)

### Save an entity profile {#save-profile}

Saves the entity's profile, replacing any it had. Send a profile document:

```json
{
  "semantic_profile": { },
  "privacy_classification": { }
}
```

You can also send a bare semantic profile. The `stored` field of a read has the same shape. Phoenix stamps the document with the current schema version, and saves it with origin `user` when it names none.

To create a profile without overwriting one, send the header `If-None-Match: *`. If the entity already has a profile, nothing is saved and you get `412`.

The entity ID in the path must be a domain, a dot, then lower-case letters, digits and underscores. Use the same form for reads and deletes.

The response is `{ entity_id, stored, warnings }`. `warnings` lists the trigger issues MESA finds for this entity, in the shape described in [Issues and the tag vocabulary](guide:#issues).

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.badEntityId` | The entity ID has the wrong form. |
| 412 | `precondition_failed` | `adminError.mesaProfileExists` | You sent `If-None-Match: *` and a profile already exists. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | none, `message_passthrough` | MESA refused the document. The message is MESA's own. |

### Delete an entity profile {#delete-profile}

Removes the entity's own profile, so it follows the levels above it again. The response is `{ entity_id, "deleted": true }`, also when there was no profile.

## Profiles at other levels {#scope-profiles}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/devices
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/devices/{device_id}
PUT    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/devices/{device_id}
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/devices/{device_id}
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/device-options
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/areas
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/areas/{area_id}
PUT    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/areas/{area_id}
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/areas/{area_id}
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/integrations
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/integrations/{integration}
PUT    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/integrations/{integration}
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/integrations/{integration}
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/integration-options
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/domains
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/domains/{domain}
PUT    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/domains/{domain}
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/domains/{domain}
```

Use these for profiles that cover a device, an area, an integration or a domain. They work like entity profiles, with a different key.

| Level | Key in the response | Key format on save | Error for a bad key |
|---|---|---|---|
| Device | `device_id` | At most 255 characters, none of `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, `&` or `;` | `adminError.nodeIdTooLong`, `adminError.nodeIdInvalidChars` |
| Area | `area_id` | At most 255 characters, none of `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, `&` or `;` | `adminError.nodeIdTooLong`, `adminError.nodeIdInvalidChars` |
| Integration | `integration` | A lower-case letter, then lower-case letters, digits and underscores | `adminError.integrationNameInvalid` |
| Domain | `domain` | A lower-case letter, then lower-case letters, digits and underscores | `adminError.badDomain` |

Related: [IDs in paths](guide:topic.adminApi#ids)

### Lists {#scope-lists}

Each list answers with one array named after its level, sorted by key: `{ devices }`, `{ areas }`, `{ integrations }` or `{ domains }`. Each item is `{ <key>, document }`, such as `{ device_id, document }`. These lists don't page.

### Read, save and delete {#scope-profile}

- A read answers `{ <key>, stored }`, with `stored` set to `null` when there's no profile. Only entity reads add `effective` and `explanation`.
- A save takes the same document and `If-None-Match: *` header as [Save an entity profile](guide:#save-profile). It answers `{ <key>, stored }`, without `warnings`.
- A delete answers `{ <key>, "deleted": true }`, also when there was no profile.
- Only saves check the key format.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | the key's error from the table above | The key has the wrong form. Saves only. |
| 412 | `precondition_failed` | `adminError.mesaProfileExists` | You sent `If-None-Match: *` and a profile already exists. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | none, `message_passthrough` | MESA refused the document. The message is MESA's own. |

### Picker lists {#picker-lists}

These list what you can give a profile to, for a picker in your own app. They work while MESA is off.

- `device-options` answers `{ devices: [{ id, name }] }`, sorted by name. The name is the user's own name for the device, else its device name, else its ID.
- `integration-options` answers `{ integrations: [{ id, name }] }`: every integration that created entities, except Phoenix MCP itself.

## Deployment defaults {#defaults}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/defaults
PUT    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/defaults
```

Use these to read and set what MESA applies to entities that have no profile at any level. Deployment defaults are three settings, not a profile document.

Related: [The built-in baseline](guide:topic.mesaRules#baseline)

### Read the defaults {#read-defaults}

MESA's own format wraps the settings a second time, so the response nests `deployment_defaults` twice. The outer one is `null` when no defaults are stored:

```json
{
  "deployment_defaults": {
    "deployment_defaults": {
      "default_control_mode": "confirm",
      "triggers_automations_domains": [],
      "domain_overrides": {}
    }
  }
}
```

### Set the defaults {#set-defaults}

Send `{ "deployment_defaults": { ... } }`, or the inner object alone, with only these keys:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `default_control_mode` | string | `autonomous`, `confirm`, `read_only` or `prohibited`. Default `confirm`. |
| `triggers_automations_domains` | array of strings | Domains, as strings. |
| `domain_overrides` | object | Keyed by domain. Each value is an object. |

The response has the same shape as a read.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.deploymentDefaultsInvalid` | MESA refused the defaults. `message_params.detail` says why. |

## Issues and the tag vocabulary {#issues}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/vocabulary
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/issues
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/orphans/clear
```

Use these to read the tags MESA knows, find profiles that disagree with your automations, and clean up profiles left behind by removed items.

### Vocabulary {#vocabulary}

Answers `{ canonical_tags, canonical_roots }`, both sorted. It works while MESA is off.

### Issues, orphans and suggestions {#read-issues}

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `refresh` | query, string | Leave it out for the stored lists. `suggestions` recomputes suggestions only. Any other value recomputes everything. |

The response is `{ issues, orphans, orphan_devices, orphan_areas, orphan_integrations, suggestions, dismissed_suggestions }`.

- An issue is `{ entity_id, declared_value, automation_id, role, severity, recommendation }`.
- Suggestions have the same shape, plus a `key` you use to dismiss or restore them.
- The orphan lists name profiles whose entity, device, area or integration no longer exists.

### Clear orphans {#clear-orphans}

Deletes every orphaned entity, device, area and integration profile. Send no body. Phoenix checks the orphans against Home Assistant first, then deletes exactly those profiles.

The response is `{ deleted: { entities, devices, areas, integrations }, count }`.

## Import and export {#portability}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/export
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/import
```

Use these to copy every MESA profile, and the deployment defaults, to a file and back.

### Export {#export}

Returns every profile as one archive:

```json
{
  "mesa_export": {
    "format_version": "1.1",
    "exported_at": "...",
    "mesa_core_version": "...",
    "entities": {},
    "domains": {},
    "integrations": {},
    "areas": {},
    "devices": {},
    "deployment_defaults": {},
    "unreadable_profiles": []
  }
}
```

Each section maps a profile's key to its document. `deployment_defaults` appears only when defaults are stored. A stored profile that MESA can't read is left out, and its key is listed in `unreadable_profiles`, which appears only then.

### Import {#import}

Checks every profile in an archive and saves the valid ones. Phoenix never saves an invalid profile; it reports it instead. Afterwards it recomputes orphans and suggestions.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `archive` | object | Required. An export, with `mesa_export` at the root and `format_version` `1.0` or `1.1`. |
| `on_conflict` | string | `skip` (default) keeps profiles you already have. `overwrite` replaces them. |

The response is `{ imported, overwritten, skipped_existing, invalid }`:

- `imported` and `overwritten` are counts.
- `skipped_existing` lists the profiles kept because they already existed.
- `invalid` maps each refused profile to the reason.
- Profiles are named `<section>:<key>`, such as `entities:light.kitchen`, or `deployment_defaults`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.mesaArchiveRequired` | `archive` is missing. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.mesaConflictModeInvalid` | `on_conflict` is something other than `skip` or `overwrite`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | none, `message_passthrough` | The archive isn't a MESA export, or its `format_version` isn't supported. |

## Suggestions {#suggestions}

```
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/suggestions/dismiss
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/mesa/suggestions/restore
```

Use these to hide a profile suggestion you don't want, or bring dismissed ones back. Read the suggestions themselves from [Issues, orphans and suggestions](guide:#read-issues).

Related: [Suggestions](guide:window.mesaSuggestions)

### Dismiss a suggestion {#dismiss-suggestion}

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Required, not empty. The `key` of a suggestion in the current list. |

The response is `{ dismissed, suggestions, dismissed_suggestions }`, where `dismissed` is the key.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.suggestionKeyRequired` | `key` is missing or empty. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.suggestionNotCurrent` | No current suggestion has this key. |

### Restore suggestions {#restore-suggestion}

Send `key` for one dismissed suggestion, or `all: true` for every one.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | The key of one dismissed suggestion. |
| `all` | boolean | `true` restores every dismissed suggestion. |

The response is `{ restored, suggestions, dismissed_suggestions }`. `restored` is the key, or with `all`, how many dismissals were cleared.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.suggestionRestoreTargetRequired` | Neither `key` nor `all: true` was sent. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.suggestionNotDismissed` | That key isn't dismissed. |

topic.adminApiSettings.title: Settings and System Endpoints
topic.adminApiSettings.body:
Use these endpoints to read and change Phoenix's global settings, clear its data, and read its logs, version and routing counters. Every endpoint follows the rules in the [Admin API](guide:topic.adminApi) overview.

Related: [Errors](guide:topic.adminApi#errors), [Agent Chat Endpoints](guide:topic.adminApiChat)

## Settings {#settings}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/settings
PATCH  /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/settings
```

Read and change the settings behind the Settings workspace. For what each setting means to an operator, see its window page: [General](guide:window.settingsGeneral), [Safety](guide:window.settingsSafety), [Logs](guide:window.settingsLogs), [Agent Chat](guide:window.settingsChat), [Home Assistant](guide:window.settingsHome) and [AI providers](guide:window.settingsProviders).

### Read settings {#settings-read}

`GET /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/settings` returns every [writable setting](guide:#writable-settings) plus these read-only fields:

- `tool_routing_qualified_languages`
- `assist_api_supported`
- `voice_agent_pipeline_supported`
- `voice_agent_pipeline_preferred`
- `voice_agent_pipeline_id`, set only by the [Voice Agent assistant](guide:#voice-pipeline) routes
- `ai_task_supported`
- `ai_task_decisions_supported`
- `esphome_integration`, `esphome_builder` and `esphome_builder_live`

### Change settings {#settings-change}

`PATCH /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/settings` takes any subset of the writable settings. No setting needs a confirmation field, not even `kill_switch`.

Phoenix checks every value before it writes anything. The first problem rejects the whole request, and nothing changes.

An accepted change has these effects:

- It cancels decision work in progress, and invalidates routing results and command approvals still in flight.
- Turning `access_key_presets_enabled` on gives every key a Default preset.
- Turning `kill_switch` off opens the agent routes again.
- Phoenix applies `mesa_mode` straight away, and updates the Voice Agent, AI Task and Assist Tool Provider.
- `mesa_inject_enabled` and `agentcli_global` take effect on the next full page load.

The audit log records the change with the names of the changed settings, not their values. The response is the same as for a read. It adds `voice_agent_pipeline_kept: true` when the Voice Agent is no longer fully set up, but Home Assistant kept Phoenix's assistant as its only one.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.unknownFields` | A field isn't writable, such as `voice_agent_pipeline_id`. `message_params` has `fields`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.booleanRequired` | A boolean setting got another type. `message_params` has `field`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.valueAllowed` | A choice setting got another value: `mesa_mode`, a style, a detail level, a routing mode or an audit menu. `message_params` has `field` and `values`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.integerRequired` | An integer setting got another type. `message_params` has `field`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.routingLanguagesInvalid` | `command_routing_languages` names a language that isn't an installed Assist language. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.conversationLimitInvalid` | A Conversation Log limit, `command_routing_timeout_ms`, `decision_timeout_ms` or `decision_request_budget` is out of range. `message_params` has `field`, `min` and `max`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.accessKeyIdOrNull` | An access key setting isn't a string or `null`. `message_params` has `field`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.activeAccessKeyRequired` | An access key setting doesn't name an active key. `message_params` has `field`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.stringOrNull` | A model setting isn't a string or `null`. `message_params` has `field`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.configuredProviderRequired` | A provider setting names no existing account. `message_params` has `field`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.decisionProviderRequired` | A decision feature was turned on with no decision account. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.toolRoutingUnqualified` | A tool review mode was set to `advise` for a model with no qualified language. |

### Writable settings {#writable-settings}

"Rejected" means an out-of-range value answers `400`. "Clamped" means Phoenix moves it to the nearest bound. A "decision account" is an account of the decision kind, and a "conversation account" any other.

| Setting | Type and range | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

## Settings without a panel control {#api-only}

The panel has no control for these settings and values. Set them only through the API.

- `agentcli_routing_mode` `local` and `hybrid`: the panel shows either as on. `hybrid` needs a decision account.
- `voice_agent_routing_mode` `local_shadow`, `local` and `hybrid`. `auto` itself works as `hybrid` while a decision account is in use, and as `local` otherwise.
- `agentcli_routing_shadow_enabled`: runs Agent Chat command recognition as observation only, while chat routing is off. Any change that sets either routing mode to `off` or `auto` turns it off.
- `command_routing_languages`: the languages for `local_shadow`, `local`, `hybrid` and background observation, from the installed Assist sentence languages plus `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant`. `auto` uses every installed Assist language instead.
- `command_routing_timeout_ms`: how long local recognition may take, in milliseconds.
- `decision_shadow_enabled`: sends Voice Agent commands that recognition missed to the decision provider, as observation only. It works only with `voice_agent_routing_mode` `local` or `local_shadow`.

The three tool review modes ask the decision provider to check each tool call the model proposes, before it runs. They are `agentcli_tool_routing_mode`, `voice_agent_tool_routing_mode` and `ai_task_tool_routing_mode`.

- `observe` and `advise` need a decision account.
- `advise` also needs a qualified language. `tool_routing_qualified_languages` lists them; while it's empty, Phoenix refuses `advise` with `adminError.toolRoutingUnqualified`.
- Home Companion keys skip tool review.

Related: [How a command is routed](guide:topic.commandRouting)

## Wiping data {#wipe}

```
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/wipe
```

Deletes Phoenix's data, by scope. This can't be undone.

```json
{"confirm": "WIPE", "wipe_core": true, "wipe_providers": true, "wipe_mesa": false}
```

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `confirm` | string | Required. Exactly `"WIPE"`. |
| `wipe_core` | boolean | Default `true`. |
| `wipe_providers` | boolean | Default `true`. |
| `wipe_mesa` | boolean | Default `false`. |

A missing flag, or one that isn't a boolean, uses its default. So `{"confirm": "WIPE"}` alone wipes core data and provider accounts.

`wipe_core` clears:

- Access keys, archived keys, entity hints, and every setting back to its default.
- Pending approvals. Phoenix dismisses their notifications and reports them resolved.
- The audit log, the Conversation Log, version history and the journal of agent writes with an unknown outcome.
- Routing statistics, the decision request count, the card catalog cache and routing clarifications.
- Rate limit counts, request counters and notification markers.
- Per-key sensors and expiry timers. Phoenix also puts back any integration log level an agent changed for a limited time.
- The Phoenix Assist pipeline.

Afterwards, Phoenix applies each changed default, such as MESA mode, the Voice Agent, AI Task and the modules added to Home Assistant's pages. It opens the agent routes if they were off.

`wipe_providers` clears every Agent Chat and decision account, with their API keys. It also clears the settings that use them. That's the Voice Agent and AI Task provider and model, and the decision account in use and its default. Shadow observation, tool review and every `hybrid` mode turn off too.

`wipe_mesa` clears every MESA profile and dismissed suggestion.

No flag clears configuration recovery records, the calendar write journal or dashboard resource records. Remove a resolved recovery record with its own endpoint.

The response is `204` with no body.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.wipeConfirmationRequired` | `confirm` isn't exactly `"WIPE"`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.approvalWipeInProgress` | An approval is running. Wait for it to finish. Only with `wipe_core`. |
| 409 | `conflict` | `adminError.approvalWipeExecutionUncertain` | An approval may have applied without reporting back. Check its result first. Only with `wipe_core`. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.mesaSaveFailed` | Phoenix couldn't save the MESA change. Only with `wipe_mesa`. |

Related: [Safety settings](guide:window.settingsSafety#data-management)

### Confirmation fields {#confirmations}

Only three routes ask for a confirmation in the body. The settings PATCH asks for none.

| Route | Body |
|---|---|
| [Wipe data](guide:#wipe) | `{"confirm": "WIPE"}` plus optional scope flags |
| [Clear the Conversation Log](guide:#clear-conversations) | Exactly `{"confirm": true}` |
| [Reset routing statistics](guide:#reset-statistics) | Exactly `{"surface": "voice", "confirm": true}`, or `"chat"` |

## Version and tools {#info}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/info
```

Returns Phoenix's version and what it offers agents.

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `version` | Phoenix's version. |
| `min_ha_version` | The oldest Home Assistant version Phoenix supports. |
| `github_url` | The project's repository. |
| `tool_count` | `total`, `native` and `additional`, counted from the full tool catalog, whatever is turned on. |
| `home_companion_reach` | `control_domains`, `read_domains` and `sensor_classes` for Home Companion keys. |

## Panel strings {#catalog}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/catalog/{language}
```

Returns the panel's strings for one language. It answers while Phoenix is still starting, unlike every other endpoint.

The response is `{"language": "<code>", "resources": {...}}`, with flat dotted keys. Phoenix picks the closest language it ships, then falls back to English. An unknown language answers English with `"language": "en"`. Strings that aren't translated, or whose placeholders don't match, come back in English.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.catalogNotFound` | No catalog was found. This happens only if the English catalog is missing. |

## Audit log {#audit}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/audit
```

Pages through the log of agent requests, newest first.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | Default 100, at most 500. |
| `offset` | integer | See [Request bodies](guide:topic.adminApi#bodies). |
| `access_key_id` | string | Exact match. |
| `outcome` | string | Exact match: `allowed`, `denied`, `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `not_implemented`, `invalid_request`, `pending_approval`, `cancelled` or `unknown`. |
| `ip` | string | Part of the client address. |
| `method` | string | Part of the method, any case. |
| `resource` | string | Part of the resource, any case. |
| `request_id` | string | Exact match. |
| `since` | string | An ISO time. A time without a zone counts as local time. |

The response has `entries` and `total`. Each entry has `request_id`, `timestamp`, `access_key_id`, `access_key_name`, `method`, `resource`, `outcome`, `client_ip` and `pass_through`. It may also have `payload`, `mesa_advisory`, `preset`, `stale_tools_advisory`, `ha_user_id` and `originating_access_key_id`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.badPagination`, `adminError.paginationNonNegative` | `limit` or `offset` isn't a whole number of 0 or more. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.sinceTimestampInvalid` | `since` isn't a valid time. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.outcomeFilterUnknown` | `outcome` isn't one of the values above, or is empty. `message_params` has `value`. |

Related: [{{label:shell.tabAudit}}](guide:window.auditLog), [Log records](guide:topic.logRecords)

## Conversation Log {#conversations}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/conversations
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/conversations
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/conversations/{entry_id}
```

Read and clear the recorded conversations. Turn recording on with `conversation_log_enabled`.

Related: [Conversation Log](guide:window.conversationLog)

### List conversations {#list-conversations}

`GET /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/conversations`

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | Default 25, at most 100. |
| `offset` | integer | See [Request bodies](guide:topic.adminApi#bodies). |
| `search` | string | At most 512 characters. Matches recorded content, any case. |
| `source` | string | At most 64 characters: `mcp`, `agentcli`, `assist`, `voice`, `ai_task` or `home_companion`. |
| `outcome` | string | At most 64 characters. A status value. `failed` and `denied` also match turns with mixed results. |
| `since` | string | An ISO time. A time without a zone counts as local time. |
| `grouped` | string | Set to `true` for grouped rows. |

The response has `entries`, `total`, `enabled`, `available`, `bytes` and `max_bytes`. Entries are newest first.

Each entry has `id`, `source`, `started_at`, `updated_at`, `finished_at`, `coverage`, `status` and `execution_status`. It also has `response_status`, `tool_count`, `change_count`, `omissions`, `omitted_events`, `first_tool`, `excerpt` and `prompt_attachments`.

Grouped entries also have `latest_at`. Agent Chat threads add `turns`, oldest first, and `history_missing`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.badPagination`, `adminError.paginationNonNegative` | `limit` or `offset` isn't a whole number of 0 or more. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.sinceTimestampInvalid` | `since` isn't a valid time. |

### Open a conversation {#open-conversation}

`GET /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/conversations/{entry_id}` returns the full stored record, with its events and the reasons anything was left out.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.conversationNotFound` | No conversation has this ID, or it has expired. |

### Clear the Conversation Log {#clear-conversations}

`DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/conversations` takes exactly `{"confirm": true}` and answers `{"cleared": true}`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.conversationClearConfirm` | The body isn't exactly `{"confirm": true}`. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | `adminError.conversationStorageUnavailable` | The log was cleared in memory, but saving failed. Try again. |

## Voice Agent assistant {#voice-pipeline}

```
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/voice_agent/pipeline
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/voice_agent/pipeline
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/voice_agent/pipeline/preferred
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/voice_agent/pipeline/preferred
```

Create and remove a Home Assistant assistant that uses the Phoenix Voice Agent, and choose whether it's the preferred one.

Related: [Home Assistant settings](guide:window.settingsHome#voice-assistant)

### Create the assistant {#create-pipeline}

`POST /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/voice_agent/pipeline`

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `preferred` | boolean | Optional. Default `true`. Makes the assistant Home Assistant's preferred one. |

Set up the Voice Agent fully first: enabled, with an access key, a provider and a model. If Phoenix's assistant still exists, Phoenix reuses it.

The response has `pipeline_id`, `name` and `preferred`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.booleanRequired` | `preferred` isn't a boolean. |
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.setupMissing` | Phoenix isn't set up. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.assistPipelineUnavailable` | Home Assistant has no assistant support. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.voiceAgentNotConfigured` | The Voice Agent isn't fully set up and turned on. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.assistPipelineFailed` | Creating the assistant failed. |

### Remove the assistant {#remove-pipeline}

`DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/voice_agent/pipeline` moves the preference to another assistant if needed, then deletes Phoenix's. The response is `{"ok": true, "kept": false}`.

`kept` is `true` when Home Assistant still has the assistant, because it's the only one or deleting it failed.

### Preferred assistant {#preferred-pipeline}

`POST` makes Phoenix's assistant the preferred one, and `DELETE` stops it being preferred but keeps it. Neither takes a body. The response has `pipeline_id` and `preferred`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.assistPipelineUnavailable` | Home Assistant has no assistant support. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.assistantSetupFirst` | There's no Phoenix assistant yet. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.assistantOnlyOneStaysPreferred` | Phoenix's is the only assistant, so it stays preferred. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.assistantPreferredFailed` | Saving the preference failed. |

## AI Task default {#ai-task}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/ai_task/preferred
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/ai_task/preferred
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/ai_task/preferred
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/ai_task/evaluate_preferred
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/ai_task/evaluate_preferred
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/ai_task/evaluate_preferred
```

Read and set Home Assistant's default data generation entity. `POST` makes Phoenix's AI Task entity the default, replacing any other. `DELETE` clears the default only if it's Phoenix's.

All three answer with the same fields:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `supported` | Whether Home Assistant supports AI Task. |
| `entity_id` | Phoenix's AI Task entity, or `null` until AI Task is fully set up. |
| `gen_data_entity_id` | The current default entity. |
| `gen_data_name` | The current default's name. |
| `is_preferred` | Whether Phoenix's entity is the default. |

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `not_found` | `adminError.setupMissing` | Phoenix isn't set up. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.aiTaskNotConfigured` | `POST` only. Phoenix's AI Task isn't fully set up and turned on. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.aiTaskPreferencesUnavailable` | `POST` only. Home Assistant has nowhere to save the default. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.aiTaskPreferredFailed` | `POST` only. Saving the default failed. |

Related: [Home Assistant settings](guide:window.settingsHome#ai-task-default)

## Command routing {#routing}

```
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/command-routing/preview
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/command-routing/preview
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/command-routing/statistics
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/command-routing/statistics
```

Test how Phoenix would route a sentence, and read the routing counters and totals.

Related: [How a command is routed](guide:topic.commandRouting), [Reading routing statistics](guide:topic.routingStatistics)

### Live counters {#routing-counters}

`GET /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/command-routing/preview` returns counters kept in memory. They start again from zero when Phoenix restarts.

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `observations`, `candidates`, `reasons`, `mean_elapsed_ms`, `agent_chat` | Voice recognition counters. |
| `decision_shadow` | Decision counters: `observations`, `reasons`, `choices`, `busy`, `requests`, `tool_routing`, `mean_elapsed_ms`, `hybrid`, `chat_hybrid` and `agent_chat`. |
| `request_budget` | `limit`, `used`, `remaining` (`null` when unlimited), `reset_at` and `available`. `reset_at` is in Unix seconds, at the start of the next UTC hour. |

### Test a sentence {#routing-preview}

`POST /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/command-routing/preview` shows how Phoenix would route one sentence, without running it. It counts no observation.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `access_key_id` | string | Required. An active access key. |
| `sentence` | string | Required. Not blank, at most 512 characters. |
| `language` | string | Default `en`. Any installed Assist language, including regional and Chinese script variants. |
| `decision` | boolean | Also asks the decision provider. |
| `targets` | boolean | Needs `decision`. |
| `batch` | boolean | Needs `decision` and `targets`, and no `messages`. |
| `numeric` | boolean | Needs `batch`. |
| `messages` | list | Earlier turns, for history review. Needs `decision` and no `targets`. |
| `references` | boolean | Needs `messages`. |

No other fields are allowed. Any option that needs `decision` contacts the decision account and counts against `decision_request_budget`.

The response has `route` (`local_candidate` or `provider`), `reason`, `proposal`, `executed: false`, `elapsed_ms`, `voice_observations` and `decision_observations`. Depending on the options, it also has `decision_shadow`, `batch_review` or `context_review`.

If the key or the settings change during the test, the result is `route: provider` with `reason: authority_changed`.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.routingPreviewInvalid` | A field is missing, too long, of the wrong type, not allowed, or in a combination that isn't allowed. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.activeAccessKeyRequired` | `access_key_id` doesn't name an active key. `message_params` has `field`. |

### Routing statistics {#routing-statistics}

`GET /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/command-routing/statistics` returns saved totals, kept across restarts. The response has `voice` and `chat`, each with:

- `since`
- `outcomes`: `local`, `decision`, `provider`, `pending`, `failed` and `cancelled`
- `provider_turns`
- `decision_usage` and `provider_usage`, each with `requests`, `reports`, `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`

### Reset statistics {#reset-statistics}

`DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp/admin/command-routing/statistics` resets one surface's totals:

```json
{"surface": "voice", "confirm": true}
```

Set `surface` to `voice` or `chat`. The response shows both surfaces after the reset. The decision request count isn't reset.

| Status | `error` | `message_key` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `adminError.routingStatisticsResetInvalid` | The body isn't exactly a valid `surface` with `confirm: true`. |

topic.agentEndpoints.title: Agent Endpoints
topic.agentEndpoints.body:
Agents reach Phoenix through these routes with a Phoenix access key (`phx_...`), not a Home Assistant token. This page is for developers building an MCP client or checking one.

Related: [Connecting External Apps](guide:topic.connecting), [Access keys](guide:topic.security#keys)

## Routes {#routes}

```
POST   /api/phoenix-mcp
DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/context
GET    /api/phoenix-mcp/skill
```

Agents send MCP requests to the first route, read their key's context from the second, and fetch the skill guide from the last.

- POST and DELETE also work with a trailing slash, `/api/phoenix-mcp/`.
- `GET /api/phoenix-mcp` answers `405`, since the endpoint has no GET handler.
- While the kill switch is on, these routes don't serve agents.

## Sending the key {#bearer}

Send the key in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer phx_...`. The key is `phx_` followed by 64 characters. Never put it in the URL: a `token` or `access_token` query parameter is refused even when the header is right.

Every route but the skill checks the key, in this order:

| Status | `error` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | Phoenix is starting or shutting down. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | The kill switch is on. |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | The URL has a `token` or `access_token` query parameter. |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | The `Authorization` header doesn't start with `Bearer `. |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | The value isn't `phx_` followed by 64 characters. |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | No key has this value. |
| 401 | `unauthorized` | The key is revoked or has expired. An expired key moves to the archive. |
| 429 | `rate_limited` | The key is over its rate limit. See [Rate limits](guide:#rate-limit). |

Every `401` carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Phoenix MCP"`. A key that passes gets its `last_used_at` updated before the rate limit check.

Errors on these routes have a simpler body than the admin API's: `error` and `message`, sometimes with a `suggestions` array. They carry `X-Phoenix-Request-ID` but no `message_key` and no `Cache-Control`.

```json
{ "error": "unauthorized", "message": "Unauthorized." }
```

Related: [Errors](guide:topic.adminApi#errors)

## Browser origins {#origin}

The MCP endpoint refuses requests from web pages on other sites, on both POST and DELETE. A request whose `Origin` header isn't one of Home Assistant's own URLs answers `403` with `forbidden` and the message "Origin not allowed." Phoenix checks this before the key.

Desktop and command-line apps send no `Origin`, so this doesn't affect them. The context route doesn't check the origin.

## The MCP endpoint {#mcp}

`POST /api/phoenix-mcp` takes one JSON-RPC message, or a batch, of up to 1 MiB. Phoenix supports protocol revisions `2026-07-28` and `2025-03-26`. Revision `2025-03-26` is called legacy below.

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | JSON-RPC result | A request succeeded. |
| 202 | None | The message was a notification. |
| 400 | JSON-RPC error `-32700` | The body is empty or isn't valid JSON. |
| 400 | JSON-RPC error `-32600` | The body isn't a JSON object or batch. |
| 200 | JSON-RPC error `-32601` | Legacy: the method doesn't exist. |
| 404 | Error | `2026-07-28`: the method doesn't exist. |
| 400 | JSON-RPC error `-32600` | A batch under `2026-07-28`, a legacy batch that's too big or empty, or a legacy batch with no request where a message was refused. |
| 413 | `request_too_large` | The body is over 1 MiB. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | The body can't be read, or hasn't finished arriving after 30 seconds. |
| 403 | `forbidden` | The `Origin` isn't allowed. |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | Phoenix isn't ready yet. |

A protocol header that doesn't match the request answers JSON-RPC error `-32020`. An unsupported protocol version answers `-32022`.

To get the response as a stream, send `Accept: text/event-stream`. Phoenix sends the single response as one SSE `message` event, with a keepalive every 15 seconds while it works.

### Batches {#batches}

Only legacy requests may be batches. Phoenix refuses a batch with `400` and `-32600` when it has more than 50 items, more than the key's burst, or more than its per-minute limit.

Phoenix charges the whole batch against the rate limit before running it. When too little of the limit is left, the batch answers `429` with `rate_limited` and `Retry-After`, and nothing in it runs.

### Legacy sessions {#sessions}

Under the legacy revision, `initialize` returns an `Mcp-Session-Id` header. Send it on every later request.

- Phoenix holds at most 256 sessions in all and 8 per key.
- A session closes after one hour without use, or after 60 seconds if it never finishes initializing.
- When the session limit is reached, Phoenix closes the key's least recently used idle session.
- When none is idle, the request answers `429` with JSON-RPC error `-32000` and `Retry-After`.
- An unknown `Mcp-Session-Id` answers `404` with `-32000`. A missing one answers `400`.

When the key's own sessions are all busy, `Retry-After` is 5 seconds. Otherwise it's the time until the stalest session expires, at least 5 seconds.

### Ending a session {#end-session}

`DELETE /api/phoenix-mcp` closes a legacy session. It runs the same readiness, origin and key checks as POST, including the rate limit. The response is `204` with no body.

| Status | `error` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | The `Mcp-Session-Id` header is missing. |
| 404 | `not_found` | The session doesn't exist, has expired or belongs to another key. |

## Context {#context}

`GET /api/phoenix-mcp/context` describes what the key can reach. It answers in plain text by default; add `?format=json` for JSON. It runs the key check and the rate limit, and every call goes in the audit log.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `access_key_name` | string | |
| `pass_through` | boolean | |
| `persona` | string | |
| `notes` | string or null | The key's notes. |
| `entities` | array | Each has `entity_id`, `permission` (`READ` or `READ/WRITE`), `area_id` and, when set, `hint`. |
| `capability_flags` | object | The capability values that apply to the agent. |
| `rate_limit` | object | `requests_per_minute` and `burst_per_second`. |

A Home Companion key gets only `access_key_name`, `persona`, an empty `entities`, `capability_flags` and `message`.

## Skill {#skill}

`GET /api/phoenix-mcp/skill` answers with the Phoenix MCP skill guide as Markdown (`text/markdown`). It needs no key, isn't rate limited and holds nothing about your home. It's the same for everyone.

While Phoenix is starting or shutting down, or the kill switch is on, it answers `503` with the plain text "Service unavailable." Its responses carry no `X-Phoenix-Request-ID`.

Related: [What the agent is told](guide:topic.connecting#primer)

## Rate limits {#rate-limit}

Each key has two limits. `rate_limit_requests` counts requests over a sliding 60 seconds. `rate_limit_burst` counts requests in any one second; 0 turns the burst limit off. A `rate_limit_requests` of 0 turns both off.

Related: [{{label:accessKeys.cardRateLimiting}}](guide:window.keySettings#rate-limiting)

### Limit headers {#limit-headers}

Successful MCP responses tell the agent where it stands:

```http
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 47
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1793612345
```

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | The key's `rate_limit_requests`. |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the current 60 seconds, after this one. A batch counts every item. |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix time, in whole seconds, when the oldest request in the window drops out of it. |

These headers appear only on `200` JSON and SSE responses from `POST /api/phoenix-mcp`, batches included. Notifications, protocol errors, other errors, DELETE, context and skill don't get them. A key with rate limiting off gets none.

### When the limit is hit {#limit-hit}

The request answers `429` with `rate_limited` and a `Retry-After` header in seconds, at least 1. It's the time until enough old requests drop out of the minute or burst window. A `429` carries no `X-RateLimit` headers.

```json
{ "error": "rate_limited", "message": "Rate limit exceeded." }
```

Wait for `Retry-After` before you try again.

Related: [Key statistics](guide:topic.adminApiKeys#key-stats)

topic.approvalLifecycle.title: How an Approval Works
topic.approvalLifecycle.body:
What happens to a request from the moment an agent asks until it's decided, and what the agent is told along the way.

## What waits for you {#held}

A capability set to Confirm holds the changes it covers. Reads covered by the same capability run straight away.

MESA's Confirm holds an action only while MESA is Enforced. One approval covers both, so you never approve the same action twice. Configuration recovery also asks here before it puts something back.

Related: [Deny, Allow and Confirm](guide:window.capabilities#modes)

## What the agent is told {#agent}

- External apps hear at once that the request is waiting, and can ask for the outcome later. With an [inline approval wait](guide:window.keySettings#inline-wait), the app waits up to that long for your decision first.
- Agent Chat waits for your decision for up to 15 minutes. If no decision comes by then, or the chat ends first, the request is cancelled.
- The Voice Agent, Assist and AI Task don't wait: they report that the change is waiting for approval and carry on. Approving later still runs it.

## How long a request waits {#expiry}

A pending request expires after one hour. Once it has, Review offers only Reject, and rejecting it records it as expired. Each access key can have up to 100 pending requests at once.

## What happens when you approve {#approve}

Phoenix checks the request again before running it:

- An expired request closes as expired.
- If the access key was revoked or has expired, the request is cancelled.
- If its capability is now Deny, the request fails without running.
- If the kill switch is on, the request is cancelled, unless it's a configuration recovery review.

Once those pass, Phoenix records your decision before it runs anything. Each action also checks its own targets, permissions and MESA rules again. If the devices it targets have changed since the request, it's refused, and the agent must ask again.

A request can reach more than it names, such as a raw command that works on a whole device. It lists the rest as `also_reaches`, and those entities count as targets.

## How it can end {#outcomes}

- Approved: it ran, and its result is saved.
- Failed: it was refused at the last check, or the action returned an error. It isn't offered again.
- Interrupted: it stopped while running, or Phoenix couldn't confirm the result, so it may have partly applied. Check the result yourself.

Only a failure before the action starts leaves the request pending, to approve again.

## Rejecting {#reject}

The agent receives your reason, or is told to ask you if you gave none. A rejected configuration recovery keeps the current configuration.

## What ends a request early {#cancelled}

Restarting Home Assistant cancels every pending request. Reloading Phoenix doesn't, and an approved action that's already running carries on. Revoking the access key, the key expiring and deleting core data cancel its requests too. Approving while the kill switch is on cancels the request instead, except for a configuration recovery review.

An approved action that's running also carries on if you reload or close the page.

## Notifications {#notify}

With **{{label:settings.notifyApprovalLabel}}** on, each request raises a Home Assistant notification that links to it, and the notification goes away once the request is decided.

Related: [Home Assistant notifications](guide:window.settingsLogs#notify-approval)

## History {#history}

Decided requests are kept for seven days, up to the newest 500. Their arguments, change and result are cleared about an hour after the decision. Interrupted requests stay in the list, so you can check what happened, but their arguments, change and result are cleared after seven days too.

topic.commandRouting.title: How a Command Is Routed
topic.commandRouting.body:
Simple commands like "turn off the kitchen light" don't need a full AI model. When command handling is on, Phoenix tries cheaper ways first.

## The order Phoenix tries {#order}

1. Home Assistant's sentence matching, in every installed Assist language. It runs in your home and costs nothing.
2. The decision provider, if you use one. It handles the commands sentence matching missed.
3. Your AI model, for everything else, just as without command handling.

Once a step carries out a command, the later steps aren't used.

Related: [Decision provider](guide:window.settingsProviders#decision-provider)

## When it applies {#when}

You turn command handling on separately for [Agent Chat](guide:window.settingsChat#chat-commands) and the [Voice Agent](guide:window.settingsHome#voice-commands).

It only applies to plain text messages. Messages for Home Companion keys always go straight to the companion.

## Follow-up messages {#follow-ups}

The first message in a conversation can go to the decision provider. A follow-up only goes there with a TypeSafe / JEV model, in a language the model supports. Otherwise it goes to your AI model.

## Limits {#limits}

The decision provider has a time limit for each request, and an optional hourly limit. If either is reached, the command goes to your AI model, so nothing goes unanswered.

Related: [Connection settings](guide:window.settingsProviders#decision-connection)

## Seeing the effect {#effect}

Routing statistics count how each message was handled, so you can see what command handling saves you.

Related: [Reading the statistics](guide:topic.routingStatistics)

topic.configurationHistory.title: What Changes Records
topic.configurationHistory.body:
Phoenix records a change after an agent's write has succeeded, with the item before and after it. Changes approved in Approvals are recorded the same way; requests you reject record nothing.

## What is recorded {#recorded}

- Automations, scripts and scenes.
- Helpers, including zones, tags and people, and the settings of integration-based helpers.
- Dashboard layouts and the Energy dashboard.
- Blueprints.
- Entity and device registry edits, and integration names and options.
- Areas, floors, labels and categories.
- Restores from this panel, as rollbacks.

## What is not {#not-recorded}

Changes made outside Phoenix, in Home Assistant itself, aren't recorded. Neither are actions on devices, calendar events, to-do items, the dashboard list or dashboard resources.

Nothing can bring back a removed to-do item, so check the items when you approve a removal.

Some records exist only as evidence and can't be restored, such as removing an integration or a device.

## How long it's kept {#retention}

Phoenix keeps the 20 newest changes to each item, with no time limit. History survives restarts. Deleting core data in [Data Management](guide:window.settingsSafety#wipe-core) clears it.

Records hold the configuration exactly as it was, so a restore can put it back. Only administrators can see them.

## What a restore can put back {#restore}

- Automations, scripts, scenes, helpers and blueprints: edited back, or recreated under their original ID if they were deleted.
- Dashboards: the layout is put back, but a deleted dashboard isn't recreated.
- Entities and devices: their names, areas, labels and similar registry details. A deleted entity can't be recreated.
- Areas, floors, labels and categories: only while the same item still exists.
- The Energy dashboard: its whole configuration.

Restoring a helper usually replaces it whole, so fields added since are removed. A configuration that used !secret, !include or similar tags can't be restored.

## Safety copies {#recovery}

Before some risky writes, Phoenix also keeps a safety copy, separate from Changes. If a write may not have finished, Phoenix asks in Approvals whether to put the copy back. Safety copies survive deleting core data.

Phoenix won't keep a copy that holds a secret, so it refuses the change instead. For a dashboard, the agent's message names the place in the layout. Ordinary card settings such as `max_tokens` or a `session` label are fine, and the layout can nest up to 100 levels.

Phoenix checks unfinished writes every 30 seconds and at startup. It keeps up to 256 safety copies, each up to 1 MiB. Resolved copies are kept for 30 days, and at most 20 per item.

topic.connecting.title: Connecting External Apps
topic.connecting.body:
An external app, such as a coding assistant or a desktop chat app, connects to Phoenix with one access key. The app's own model does the thinking, and Phoenix decides what it may do.

## Getting the setup commands {#commands}

Phoenix shows the exact command or configuration for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI, Codex, Cursor and DeepSeek Harness, plus a general one for any other MCP app. They appear in three places:

- The **Connect** step of [{{label:accessKeys.setUpAgent}}](guide:wizard.connect).
- **{{label:accessKeys.postCreateConnectTitle}}**, right after you create a key.
- **{{label:accessKeys.helpConnect}}**, after you rotate a key.

The commands contain the key itself, which Phoenix shows only once. To see them again for an existing key, rotate it and update the app.

Each app's tab links to that app's own setup guide. Restart or reload the app afterwards.

## Keeping the key safe {#credentials}

The access key works like a password for everything its permissions allow. Phoenix stores only a fingerprint of it, so it can't show it again.

Keep it out of shared files and chat logs. The setup commands for Claude Code, Gemini and Codex put it on the command line, so clear your shell history if others can read it. If it leaks, [rotate](guide:window.accessKeys#rotate) the key: the old value stops working straight away.

## Using several keys {#several-keys}

Give each app or task its own key, with only the permissions it needs. Each key gets its own server name in the app, such as phx-home, so one app can hold several keys side by side.

Renaming a key keeps it working, but new setup commands use the new name.

## The connection {#connection}

Apps connect to your Home Assistant address followed by /api/phoenix-mcp, sending the key as a bearer token. The URL in the setup commands is the one your browser uses; change it there if the app reaches Home Assistant another way.

Phoenix speaks MCP over Streamable HTTP. Older app settings that use the SSE transport won't connect. Long actions keep the connection alive with a message every 15 seconds.

## Connecting from outside your home {#remote}

Phoenix has no remote service of its own. An app outside your home reaches it the same way your browser would: through your Nabu Casa address, your own domain, or a VPN such as Tailscale. Change the URL in the setup commands to that address, followed by /api/phoenix-mcp.

Use an https address outside your home, because the key travels with every request. A reverse proxy must pass the Authorization header through and allow long responses. Hosted apps connect from their provider's servers, so a home network or VPN address won't work for them.

## When the tools change {#reconnect}

Some apps read the list of tools only when they connect. After you change a key's capabilities or permissions, reconnect the app to see the new list. Phoenix also tells the agent on its next call: to reconnect when its tools changed, or, when only which actions need approval changed, that its tools are the same.

Related: [Reconnecting an agent](guide:window.accessKeys#reconnect)

## What the agent is told {#primer}

When an app connects, Phoenix sends it short instructions for working safely: how approvals and dry runs work, which actions need your approval, and the key's notes. A Home Companion key gets a shorter fixed version.

Apps that support skills can also install the Phoenix MCP skill, a longer guide shown under **{{label:wizard.skillSectionTitle}}**. It's the same for everyone and holds nothing about your home.

## Through Home Assistant's MCP Server {#ha-mcp-server}

Apps that sign in to Home Assistant itself, such as hosted connectors, can reach Phoenix's tools through Home Assistant's Model Context Protocol integration. Before 2026.11 it was called MCP Server. They use the key bound to [Assist Tool Provider](guide:topic.homeAssistantFeatures#assist-tool-provider).

On 2026.11, use /api/mcp/phoenix_mcp, which needs an administrator's sign-in. Home Assistant 2026.7 doesn't have that address, and other versions before 2026.11 may not, so use /api/mcp there.

The /api/mcp address follows that integration's Require an administrator account option. New entries turn it on, older entries keep it off, and 2026.7 has no such option. Someone who isn't an administrator gets only household tools, within their own Home Assistant rights.

On that route the key's rate limit doesn't apply, the audit log shows the calls as Assist, and the app gets Phoenix's instructions only if it asks for them.

From 2026.11, check that integration's options. A new entry serves every API, Phoenix's included, unless you choose. The read-only option leaves an app only the tools marked read-only, but it doesn't replace the key's capabilities.

Tools from Home Assistant's other APIs don't pass through Phoenix on that route, so the key, approvals, MESA and the audit log don't cover them. When two APIs offer the same tool name, Home Assistant adds a prefix such as `phoenix-mcp__`.

## When it doesn't connect {#problems}

- **Unauthorized (401)**: the key is wrong, revoked or expired, or was sent in the URL instead of the Authorization header.
- **Forbidden (403)**: a web page tried to connect from another site. Desktop and command-line apps aren't affected.
- **Too many requests (429)**: the key hit its rate limit, or has too many connections open at once. The app should wait and try again.
- **Unavailable (503)**: the kill switch is on, or Phoenix is still starting.

topic.homeAssistantFeatures.title: Voice Agent, AI Task or Assist Tool Provider
topic.homeAssistantFeatures.body:
Phoenix can work with Home Assistant's AI features in three ways. The difference is whose model answers, and what the access key controls.

## Voice Agent {#voice-agent}

Phoenix answers Home Assistant conversations itself, with your account and model. What it can do is limited by its access key, and by the permissions of the person speaking.

Use it if you want Phoenix's own model and tools behind voice and Assist.

A reply stops at 8,000 characters and says it was cut. Assist shows the same text.

## AI Task {#ai-task}

Phoenix runs Home Assistant's AI Task actions for automations and scripts, with your account and model. It acts for the household, within its access key. If Home Assistant says who started a task, the task has only that person's rights.

It can also answer Home Assistant's Evaluate action for automations and scripts: see [Decisions](guide:window.settingsHome#ai-decisions).

## Assist Tool Provider {#assist-tool-provider}

Another integration's model answers, and Phoenix only lends it tools. The bound access key decides which tools that model gets, and the Home Assistant user who asked limits them further. Phoenix runs no model here, and uses none of your credit.

Use it if you already have a conversation agent you like, and want it to reach your home through Phoenix's controls.

From Home Assistant 2026.11, a conversation keeps the tools it started with. Changed notes and permissions reach the model with its next tool call, and a tool it has lost is refused straight away. A tool you add needs a new conversation.

Related: [{{label:workspace.homeAssistant}}](guide:window.settingsHome)
